title: SOC Engineer
description:
About Merlin Group

Merlin Group operates at the intersection of cyber innovation, national security, and technology-driven transformation. With a mission to accelerate the adoption of high-impact technologies across the U.S. public sector and regulated commercial markets, Merlin is uniquely structured around three core tenets – Invest, Enable, and Scale – each designed to address a specific stage of the technology lifecycle. Together, our affiliates – Merlin Ventures, CGC, and Merlin Cyber – form a flywheel that builds enduring capability for customers, partners, and the broader cyber ecosystem, operationalizing technological advancement into mission-ready, enterprise-grade solutions.


At Merlin, we believe our strength lies in our people. Team members are encouraged to be creative, collaborative, and nimble, pursuing paths to deliver the cutting-edge cybersecurity solutions that our customers rely on. From next-generation cyber defense to secure cloud and AI, we are united by one purpose – transforming innovation into mission impact.

The Opportunity

We are looking for a SOC Engineer to build, operate, and improve the technical capabilities behind our security operations. While the role is primarily focused on security automation and platform engineering, detection engineering will play a large part as well. You will partner closely with SOC analysts to turn their needs into reliable detections, workflows, and infrastructure, and work with the SOC Manager, Engineering, Infrastructure, and GRC teams to keep the platform secure, compliant, and scalable.


Primary Duties & Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and tune detections in Splunk using SPL, mapping coverage to knowledge bases like MITRE ATT&CK and managing rules through the team's detection-as-code process with version control, testing, and peer review, while tracking false positive rates, alert volume, and coverage gaps with analysts to prioritize tuning and new content
  • Onboard, normalize, and maintain log sources and collection pipelines across AWS, Azure, and GCP, including CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Azure Activity and Entra ID logs, GCP Cloud Audit Logs, and endpoint, identity, and network telemetry, with forwarders, ingestion, retention, and integrity controls that satisfy FedRAMP audit logging requirements
  • Build and maintain Torq workflows for alert enrichment, triage, containment, and case handling, integrating with Splunk, ServiceNow, cloud provider APIs, and other SOC tools so alerts arrive as enriched ServiceNow cases with consistent fields, ownership, and SLAs, reducing analyst toil and mean time to respond
  • Engineer and operate the SOC tooling platform in AWS, including Infrastructure as Code (IaC), deployment pipelines, IAM, secrets management, and monitoring systems
  • Produce and maintain documentation, runbooks, and architecture diagrams for detections, automation playbooks, and platform components, and supply evidence for audits and control assessments
  • Serve as an engineering escalation point during incidents and participate in an on-call rotation for SOC platform issues


Qualifications

  • 4+ years of experience in SOC engineering, detection engineering, security engineering, or a closely related role
  • Deep hands-on experience with Splunk, including SPL, correlation searches, data models and CIM, knowledge object management, index and sourcetype design, and Splunk Enterprise Security
  • Experience building automation with a Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) platform (Torq strongly preferred) and integrating tools through REST APIs and webhooks
  • Proficiency in at least one scripting language, and comfort with Git-based workflows and CI/CD pipelines
  • Working knowledge of AWS services relevant to security operations (IAM, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Security Hub, Lambda, S3, VPC) and IaC tooling such as Terraform
  • Experience working with an IT Service Management (ITSM) platform (ServiceNow preferred)

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting FedRAMP Moderate or High environments or other NIST 800-53 based programs
  • Experience with detection-as-code frameworks and CI/CD for security content, such as Sigma
  • Experience configuring or integrating the ServiceNow Security Incident Response module
  • Prior work in a managed security services or multi-tenant SOC environment


Success Attributes


  • Commitment to personal and professional integrity and respect for others.
  • Roll-up-your-sleeves attitude and low-ego approach.
  • Commitment to teamwork and professional relationship development.
  • Passion for lifelong learning, growth, and development.
  • Flexible and nimble; comfortable with ambiguity and rapid change.
  • Strong communication and functional project management skills.
  • Desire to innovate, try new things, and creatively explore novel solutions to business challenges.
  • Professional and respectful approach to the diversity of thought, action, identity, and attributes.

Benefits & Perks


We want to empower and inspire employees to be and do their best. Our workdays are dynamic, collegial, and fun. Our office features multiple places to work unconstrained by typical office barriers. Our wellness package provides access to an on-site gym and includes medical, dental, and vision insurance along with options for FSA and EAP. We offer 401(k) with employer match, unlimited PTO, and a culture respectful of the reality that not everything in one’s personal life is guaranteed to happen only after hours.


All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, local, or international law.

title: AWS Cloud Platform Engineer
description:
About the company

We are a young and fast-growing recruiting company with five years of experience working across Latin America and the United States. We partner closely with teams and founders to help them build strong, high-impact teams through recruitment, outsourcing, and team-building services.

Our culture is built on effective communication, trust, and transparency. We believe great work happens when people feel heard, supported, and empowered to grow. Today, our team is made up of more than 80 professionals working across different projects throughout the region, collaborating remotely and learning from each other every day.

About the role

We’re looking for an AWS Cloud Platform Engineer to join a team building and evolving the cloud platform that supports agent-based applications.

The role covers both the AWS foundation — including accounts, networking, identity, and Infrastructure as Code — and the path from code commit to a running agent. Each engineer will have a primary focus in one of two areas while working closely across both:

Infrastructure & IaC: Build and own the AWS foundation, including accounts, networking, identity boundaries, and reusable infrastructure modules.

CI/CD & Runtime Deployment: Own the path from commit to running agent, including container builds, Amazon ECR, CI/CD pipelines, environment promotion, and AgentCore Runtime configuration.

This is a hands-on platform engineering role focused on building secure, reusable, and reliable foundations that other engineering teams can confidently use.

Responsibilities

  • Design and establish a multi-account AWS structure using AWS Organizations, Control Tower, or equivalent solutions, including guardrails and Service Control Policies.
  • Design and maintain secure VPC and networking architectures, including VPC endpoints, PrivateLink, Transit Gateway, routing, and DNS.
  • Define IAM roles, permission boundaries, and least-privilege access for platform services, pipelines, and consuming teams.
  • Build and maintain reusable, versioned Infrastructure as Code modules using Terraform and/or AWS CDK/CloudFormation.
  • Design and maintain CI/CD pipelines for building, testing, scanning, and publishing containers to Amazon ECR.
  • Automate promotion across development, testing, and production environments, including approval gates, rollback, and version tracking.
  • Configure and deploy agents to AgentCore Runtime, including session settings, scaling, configuration, and secrets management.
  • Build starter repositories, pipeline templates, and golden paths to standardize how new agents are developed and deployed.
  • Build security and compliance requirements into the platform from the beginning, including encryption, logging, tagging, image scanning, and auditability.
  • Work closely with client security teams to define and validate platform security controls.
  • Document modules, technical decisions, architecture, and operational procedures through documentation and runbooks.
  • Collaborate effectively within a blended client and vendor team, communicating technical decisions clearly and building strong working relationships.

Requirements

  • 6+ years of experience in Cloud, Platform, or DevOps Engineering, including at least 4 years of hands-on experience building production AWS environments.
  • Strong Infrastructure as Code experience with Terraform and/or AWS CDK/CloudFormation, including building reusable modules.
  • Deep knowledge of AWS IAM, including cross-account access, permission boundaries, and Service Control Policies.
  • Strong experience with AWS networking, including VPC design, routing, VPC endpoints, PrivateLink, Transit Gateway, and DNS.
  • Hands-on experience building and managing CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, AWS CodePipeline, CodeBuild, or similar tools.
  • Strong experience with Docker and Amazon ECR, plus deployment experience with ECS, EKS, Fargate, Lambda, or similar technologies.
  • Experience with AWS Secrets Manager, Parameter Store, or other secrets and configuration management solutions.
  • Deep hands-on expertise in at least one of the two focus areas, combined with working knowledge of the other.
  • Previous consulting experience.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively in blended client and vendor teams.

Nice to have

  • AWS certifications such as Solutions Architect Professional, DevOps Engineer Professional, or Advanced Networking.
  • Experience with Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore Runtime, or deploying LLM- and agent-based applications.
  • Experience with policy-as-code and software supply chain security, including OPA, Checkov, cosign, SBOM tooling, Amazon Inspector, or similar technologies.
  • Experience in pharma, life sciences, healthcare, or other regulated industries with strict security and change control requirements.
  • Previous experience and connections within the Life Sciences industry.

Benefits

  • People First culture
  • Referral Program
  • Free access to streaming platforms
  • Free access to Spotify Premium
  • GYM discount
  • Travel discount
  • E-Learning discount
  • Birthday-day gift
  • Points Program

title: Senior Technical Program Manager, ADC Security Engineering
description:
Application deadline: Oct 5, 2026

AWS Region Services delivers security and infrastructure capabilities into isolated AWS regions that support highly sensitive customer workloads. We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to drive delivery of a portfolio of regional security service programs, each involving coordination across commercial AWS service teams, regional operations, compliance organizations, and infrastructure partners.

You will own 4-6 concurrent programs at any given time, each with distinct commercial partners, compliance gates, and delivery timelines. This role requires someone who can hold multiple complex programs in their head, drive accountability across teams that don't report to you, and communicate crisp status to senior leadership weekly.

The candidate selected must obtain and maintain a security clearance at the TS/SCI with polygraph level. Upon start, the selected candidate will be sponsored for a commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.

Key job responsibilities
Own end-to-end program execution for a portfolio of security service delivery programs into isolated AWS regions
Drive cross-organizational coordination with commercial service teams who build the capabilities your programs deliver into isolated regions
Manage compliance and accreditation gates that are prerequisites for service launches in regulated environments
Build and maintain program schedules with clear critical paths, dependency tracking, and escalation triggers
Produce weekly status reporting for senior and executive leadership with quantified progress, blockers, and path to green
Identify and resolve cross-program dependencies and resource conflicts across the portfolio
Drive mechanisms and operational cadences that keep programs healthy: regular syncs with commercial partners, milestone tracking, risk registers

Must be willing and able to travel up to 20%

A day in the life
You own a portfolio of programs that deliver AWS security services into isolated regions. Monday you are pulling status across your portfolio and preparing a leadership summary. Tuesday you are in a working session with a commercial service team resolving a deployment blocker. Wednesday you are driving an accreditation review through a customer approval process. Thursday you are aligning with peer program managers on shared dependencies and resource conflicts. Friday you are reviewing program health metrics and setting up next week's priorities. Your internal stakeholders are engineering managers, commercial AWS security service teams, infrastructure delivery teams, and compliance organizations. Your customers are mission owners who need these security capabilities available in isolated regions on committed timelines.

About the team
Region Services bridges the gap between commercial AWS service teams and customers operating in isolated AWS regions. Our team delivers security services, manages infrastructure programs, and coordinates the compliance and accreditation work required to launch capabilities in high-security environments. We operate out of Denver, Arlington, and Herndon. We value direct communication, ownership of outcomes, and bias for action. Programs move through technical, operational, and compliance gates simultaneously, so the ability to manage ambiguity across multiple workstreams is essential.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

title: Director, Category Management – Data Center Electrical Infrastructure
description:
About the role

The Director, Category Management – Data Center Electrical Infrastructure leads the global end-to-end category strategy, strategic sourcing, and supplier development for mission-critical power distribution systems. In this senior role, you will manage a massive annual spend across High Voltage (HV), Medium Voltage (MV), and Low Voltage (LV) electrical equipment—including utility substations, transformers, switchgear, Uninterruptible Power Supplies (UPS), backup diesel generators, and busway systems.


Given current industry-wide constraints on long-lead electrical equipment, you will act as the primary commercial and strategic authority, securing multi-year manufacturing capacity, aligning utility and engineering roadmaps, and establishing resilient, cost-optimized supply chains to fuel rapid, hyper-scale data center expansion.


What you'll do

  • Category Strategy & Execution: Develop and execute multi-year global category strategies for HV, MV, and LV electrical commodities, balancing total cost of ownership (TCO) with critical path deployment schedules.
  • Supplier Relationship & Development: Manage executive-level relationships with Tier-1 electrical equipment OEMs and global manufacturers (e.g., switchgear, transformer, and generator suppliers). Drive capacity allocation, manufacturing footprint expansion, and performance scorecards.
  • Capacity Reservation & Long-Lead Management: Negotiate multi-year capacity reservation agreements, master supply agreements (MSAs), and framework orders to mitigate severe industry lead-time bottlenecks for critical items like step-down transformers and GIS/AIS switchgear.
  • Cross-Functional Alignment: Partner closely with Data Center Electrical Engineering, Site Selection, Energy Strategy, and Construction teams to ensure electrical topologies align with future grid requirements, high-density AI demands, and modular power designs.
  • Risk Management & Supply Resiliency: Mitigate single-point-of-failure risks across Tier-1 and Tier-2 components (e.g., electrical steel, copper windings, semiconductor chips for controls, diesel engine blocks). Develop dual-sourcing and localized manufacturing strategies.
  • Market Intelligence & Regulatory Compliance: Monitor global market trends, commodity price volatility (copper, electrical steel), utility interconnection trends, and evolving electrical codes/safety standards (e.g., IEEE, IEC, NFPA) to inform leadership decisions.

What you'll bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or a related technical discipline. Master’s degree or MBA preferred.
  • 10+ years of progressive strategic sourcing, supply chain management, or commercial operations experience, with at least 5 years specifically dedicated to data center electrical infrastructure, heavy industrial power systems, or electrical utility equipment.
  • Deep technical and commercial fluency in data center electrical distribution architectures, including HV substations, MV switchgear, backup generation (diesel/gas rotary), UPS topologies, and power distribution units (PDUs).
  • Proven track record of negotiating complex, high-stakes commercial agreements, long-lead capacity holds, and global volume purchase terms with Tier-1 electrical OEMs.
  • Strong cross-functional leadership, negotiation, and executive communication skills. Ability to influence internal engineering standards and external executive leadership alike.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Competitive Salary: $185,000 - $200,000 (commensurate with experience) + bonus + sign-on equity grant.
  • Long-Term Growth: Eligible to participate in Riot’s equity incentive programs and share in the success you help build.
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan: Incudes a generous company match.
  • Comprehensive Health Coverage: Multiple medical plan options, including 100% company-paid plans.
  • Wellness & Lifestyle Perks: Enjoy free gym memberships, pet insurance, childcare discounts, and more to support your life both in and out of work.


Riot is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

title: Licensed Clinical Social Work
description:
About the Role:

The Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) plays a critical role in providing comprehensive mental health services to individuals, families, and groups within diverse healthcare and social assistance settings. This position focuses on assessing client needs, developing personalized treatment plans, and delivering evidence-based therapeutic interventions to promote emotional well-being and social functioning. The LCSW collaborates closely with multidisciplinary teams, including medical professionals and community resources, to ensure holistic care and support for clients. Additionally, the role involves advocating for clients’ rights and access to services, while maintaining meticulous documentation to comply with regulatory standards. Ultimately, the LCSW contributes to improving the quality of life for clients by addressing complex psychosocial challenges through compassionate and professional care.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in Social Work (MSW) from an accredited program.
  • Current and valid Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) license in the state of practice within the United States.
  • Minimum of two years of post-licensure clinical experience providing direct mental health services.
  • Strong knowledge of clinical assessment, diagnosis, and evidence-based therapeutic interventions.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and adhere to ethical standards in clinical practice.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working in healthcare or social assistance settings such as hospitals, community mental health centers, or outpatient clinics.
  • Familiarity with electronic health record (EHR) systems and clinical documentation software.
  • Training or certification in specialized therapeutic approaches such as Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Trauma-Informed Care, or Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT).
  • Bilingual proficiency to serve diverse client populations effectively.
  • Experience with case management and coordination of community resources.

Responsibilities:

  • Conduct comprehensive psychosocial assessments to identify client needs, strengths, and challenges.
  • Develop, implement, and monitor individualized treatment plans based on clinical best practices and client goals.
  • Provide individual, group, and family therapy sessions using evidence-based modalities.
  • Collaborate with healthcare providers, case managers, and community organizations to coordinate care and resources.
  • Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation in compliance with legal, ethical, and organizational standards.

### Description

**Connect Adults with Stories, Resources, and Community Join the Palo Alto City Library as an Adult Services Senior Librarian**

The Palo Alto City Library is seeking an Adult Services Senior Librarian to help shape welcoming programs and services at Rinconada Library. This role focuses on adult library users, with a special emphasis on engaging Palo Alto’s older adults and retirees.

You’ll work with the Adult Services team, community partners, and colleagues across the library system to develop programs that reflect community interests and needs. You’ll also provide reference and reader services, participate in outreach, and manage designated collections at one or more branches.

**About the Library and Rinconada**

The Palo Alto City Library connects people with knowledge, resources, and opportunities for discovery. Across five branches, our staff help community members explore new interests, find reliable information, and connect with one another.

Rinconada Library offers a particularly rich setting for adult services. Located across from the Palo Alto Art Center, the branch is home to the Library’s physical Local Interest Collection and provides space for programs, learning, and community gatherings. For a Senior Librarian, it’s an opportunity to build on these resources while developing services that speak to the interests of adults and older residents.

**What You’ll Do**

- Plan, promote, and deliver programs and services for adults, including older adults and retirees.

- Build relationships with community organizations and partners to expand the library’s reach.

- Collaborate with the Adult Services team and manager to strengthen services across branches.

- Help customers discover information, library resources, and their next great read.

- Select, evaluate, and maintain designated library collections.


**Who Thrives in This Role**

We’re looking for a librarian who enjoys connecting with people, turning community interests into engaging programs, and working with others to make library services more responsive. Strong communication, collaboration, and customer service skills are essential. Experience developing programs or services for older adults is especially welcome.

**Why Palo Alto?**

Known as the birthplace of Silicon Valley, Palo Alto brings a spirit of curiosity and innovation to public service. Library staff have the chance to turn that spirit into something tangible: welcoming spaces, thoughtful collections, meaningful programs, and stronger community connections. This position offers room to bring your ideas to life while collaborating with colleagues across the library system.

**Schedule:** Sunday through Thursday, including one evening shift.

This position is represented by the Service Employees International Union (SEIU).

### Essential Duties

**Essential and other important responsibilities and duties may include, but are not limited to:**

- May perform duties of Librarian as required.

- Responsible for selection and de-selection of library materials in one or more subject areas on a rotating basis. Evaluates need to add or retain collection materials based on variety of criteria; verifies and evaluates customer requests for purchases; responsible for daily collection maintenance and evaluation; coordinates processing of discarded materials.

- Monitors physical arrangements and other requirements relevant to collection size and promotion of specific areas/collections in the library. Monitors maintenance requirements for and assists public in use of a variety of library equipment including microfilm reader printers and photocopiers, and computers.

- Responsible for security of building and safety of customers and staff.

- Responsible for all elements of library programming including planning, coordination, promotion and conducting of programs. Cooperates with other City departments, community and library groups in co-sponsorship of programs.

- Conducts reference interviews; analyzes, interprets and answers inquiries at all level of complexity utilizing resources in Palo Alto Libraries as well as other libraries and in the community, when required to meet public information needs; keeps informed of new and outdated resources; provides direct assistance to customers of all ages in location and selection of appropriate library materials and may specialize in service to children; assists customers in use of facility, materials and access tools.

- Selects, evaluates, tests, demonstrates and promotes on-line databases and other on-line products.

- Trouble-shoots problems with products in-house and remotely as needed; gathers statistics and makes recommendations based on use, value and fit in the collection.

- May assist customers with the use of library technology.

To review full job description, click [here.](https://www.governmentjobs.com/careers/paloaltoca/classspecs/793267?keywords=senior%20librarian&pagetype=classSpecifications)

Sufficient education, training and/or work experience to demonstrate possession of the following knowledge, skills and abilities, which would typically be acquired through:

- Master's Degree in Library and Information Science
- Three years professional experience as a librarian. Master's degree in Library or Information Science may be substituted for one year of professional experience.

title: Head of Enterprise Architecture & Applications
description:
Position: Head of Enterprise Architecture & ApplicationsLocation: Vaudreuil-Dorion, QCFlexible Hybrid Work Model: We support collaboration and connection through a hybrid work arrangement requiring a minimum of 3 days per week on-site.Status: Permanent, full-time (1)
Lead the architecture behind a growing North American business.

Quadra’s CRM, ERP, transportation, analytics, employee experience, regulatory compliance and AI platforms are core to how we operate across North America.

We are creating the Head of Enterprise Architecture & Applications role to unify these platforms under one architecture and delivery standard. The role leads Quadra Digital’s (QD) Design Authority pillar alongside Business Authority and Digital Workplace & Infrastructure.

Reporting to our CDIO, this visible, hands-on leader will guide the team, own the budget and investment portfolio, review designs and delivery practices, and partner with business leaders to turn priorities into measurable value.

At Quadra, we put people first so that together, we can reimagine what's possible.
For more than 50 years, Quadra has placed its 650+ employees at the heart of its success across North America. We offer an engaging culture, a collaborative and human environment, and a high level of autonomy and flexibility. Joining Quadra means being part of a professional, innovative and passionate team, within a growing, people-focused organization certified Great Place to Work®. We have also been recognized as one of Canada's Best Managed Companies for over 20 years.

A leader in the distribution of chemicals and ingredients, Quadra continues to grow with a strong commitment to its teams. If you are driven by excellence, you belong here!

Why This Role Matters:

Own enterprise architecture, business capability and process architecture, enterprise information architecture and master data governance, and AI-solution architecture and governance across CRM, ERP, transportation, analytics, employee experience and AI, as well as Quadra-critical regulatory platforms (Intelligent SDS Authoring, labelling, product stewardship and compliance).

Lead the platform managers, product owners, delivery squads, project management and QA under one intake and delivery model.

Enforce design, security, testing and release standards to make delivery predictable.

Own the digital budget and investment portfolio with Finance, the CDIO and business leaders.

Measure digital outcomes through revenue, margin, cost, service, working capital and productivity.

What would be your main responsibilities as Head of Enterprise Architecture & Applications?:

Define and govern target architecture across applications, integrations, data, security and AI; approve major designs, configurations, developments and releases.

Directly manage the platform managers, product owners, project management, QA, development and functional specialists—setting priorities, capacity, performance and development expectations.

Own delivery from qualified demand through release and Level 3 support, including application security, published SLAs and clear technical ownership.

Set and enforce delivery standards for requirements, backlogs, acceptance criteria, UAT, Jira, testing and Definition of Done.

Bring the roadmap and enhancement portfolio to the quarterly QD Prioritisation Board and provide technical validation for production changes.

Map business capabilities, processes and applications to align investments, reduce duplication and challenge proposed solutions early.

Evaluate AI and regulatory platforms (e.g., SDS authoring, labelling, product stewardship) against security, compliance, integration, data and business-value requirements.

Own digital opex and capex planning, business-case quality, stage gates and value realization with Finance, Business Authority and the relevant Key Account.

Advise business leaders on roadmap, feasibility, cost and sequencing; lead vendor selection and performance management.

Assess and integrate application landscapes acquired through mergers and acquisitions.

What are the required qualifications and experience to succeed in this role:

15+ years in enterprise/solution architecture, application management or digital delivery, including 5+ years leading specialists or Product Owners.

Bachelor’s degree in information systems, computer science, software or industrial engineering, or equivalent experience.

Proven design-authority experience across multiple platforms, including solution, integration and release approvals.

Hands-on experience with at least two of: Salesforce, Oracle JD Edwards E1 or similar ERP, Oracle OTM/TMS

Strong integration and API architecture experience across ERP, CRM and TMS in cloud or hybrid environments.

Strong business acumen and ability to translate commercial, operational and financial priorities into practical technology decisions.

Strong oral presentation skills: clear, confident communication of complex ideas, analysis outcomes, architectural concepts and design decisions—and their justification—tailored to diverse audiences and stakeholder needs.

Experience governing requirements, backlogs, Jira or Azure DevOps, SDLC controls, change management, segregation of duties and audit/compliance reviews.

Demonstrated creative thinking and ability to challenge stakeholders, defend decisions, bring stakeholders to understand and accept new approaches and deliver measurable business benefits.

Proven experience owning and managing significant technology operating and capital budgets and investment portfolios, in partnership with Finance and business leaders, with accountability for forecasting, prioritization, cost control and value realization.
Advanced written and verbal communication skills in both French and English.
Assets: MuleSoft or similar API integration platform experience; TOGAF, Zachman, AWS/Azure, Microsoft Power Platform, Power BI/Fabric, Agile/SAFe or Scrum certification; distribution, chemicals, supply chain, regulatory/product stewardship or post-acquisition integration experience.

Working Conditions

Permanent, full-time senior leadership role based in Vaudreuil-Dorion, with three full office days per week.

title: Safety Investigations Specialist III
description:
About the role and team

Customer Advocacy & Solutions at Uber is where real people solve real problems in real time. As part of the Safety Investigations team, you are a critical responder during a user’s most difficult moments. You will provide fast, empathetic support to riders, drivers, and couriers, navigating high-stakes situations where the answers aren't always clear and the emotional weight is high. This role is about more than processing tickets; it’s about making decisive calls to secure our platform and protect our community.

The environment is intense, fast-paced, and requires a steady hand. You’ll be tasked with uncovering the truth in messy, complex incidents—often dealing with conflicting statements and high-pressure timelines. We aren’t looking for someone to provide a "polished" service, but someone who can stay calm, exercise sound judgment, and act with both urgency and care. If you are resilient, detail-oriented, and motivated by the responsibility of maintaining safety at a global scale, this is where you’ll grow.

24/7 operation, must be flexible to work nights and/or weekends if needed.

Uber is not able to provide visa sponsorship for this role, must be legally authorized to work in the US.

What you’ll do

  • Navigate a high-volume caseload of urgent and critical incidents, investigating everything from accidents to sensitive safety reports with precision.
  • Conduct deep-dive investigations by analyzing evidence and interviewing involved parties—including witnesses, insurance partners, and law enforcement—to reconstruct events accurately.
  • Adjudicate driver and rider status on the platform, making the hard calls on account access based on established safety guidelines and evidence.
  • Master multiple complex knowledge bases and technical tools (like Query Builder) to document cases and manage communications across email, chat, and phone.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders, including Account Executives for business-related incidents and legal teams for attorney-involved matters.
  • Triage and resolve complex payment issues or case creation improvements, ensuring that safety incidents are tracked correctly from the first point of contact.
  • Identify patterns in safety data and provide actionable recommendations to stakeholders to prevent future incidents and improve the overall platform experience.

Basic Qualifications

  • Minimum 6 months of urgent customer support experience interviewing both parties to an incident (in-person or over the phone).

  • De-escalation, case management, stakeholder management, program management.

Preferred Qualifications

title: Regional Fraud Investigator
description:
Job Posting TitleRegional Fraud Investigator
Job Description
Regional Fraud Investigator
Job Description
Summary/Objective

The Regional Fraud Investigator position is a key role in the Fraud Investigations Unit of the Corporate Security Department. This position is responsible for conducting comprehensive external fraud investigations on check fraud, wire fraud, account take over, identity theft, new account fraud, elderly exploitation, and other types of fraud, to detect and prevent fraud losses to the bank and the customer.

They are responsible for reviewing all allegations of suspected fraud, analyzing data, making critical decisions, and interviewing witnesses, suspects, employees, and other related parties. They are responsible for reporting findings, taking the appropriate action, and effectively managing cases. Furthermore, they are responsible for the facilitation of fraud recovery, in an effort to minimize fraud losses to the bank and its customers. May perform general account handling functions such as, close account determination, holds, restraints, etc.

Routinely contacts customers and other bank team members to confirm the legitimacy of high-risk transactions prior to occurrence and takes appropriate action, to mitigate the risk to the Bank and the customer. May provide support in other investigations as assigned by the Director of Security. Will serve as liaison with the business lines, financial institution partners and law enforcement. Position role and responsibilities must be performed in adherence to the compliance of bank and department operational policies and regulations.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities include the following: Other duties and special projects may be assigned. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Investigate and manage external fraud investigations, such as check fraud, new account fraud, elder exploitation, wire fraud, online take over and other, ensuring cases are handled timely, and documented accurately with a concise case summary, following existing procedures.
  • Conduct research, compile, save and retrieve data for the preparation of investigative reports for assigned cases.
  • Review surveillance systems and extract photos/videos for use by the bank and law enforcement personnel.
  • Use internal and external resources to obtain forensic evidence for investigative purposes when reviewing fraud detection reports or investigating cases.
  • Notify and work with law enforcement and prosecutor's office regarding criminal cases to ensure proper resolution.
  • May attend criminal and civil court proceedings as necessary to complete the prosecution of cases.
  • Facilitate fraud recovery efforts to minimize losses to the bank and the customers.
  • May prepare and submit Suspicious Activity Reports SARs as required. Proper SAR determination is essential.
  • Provide business lines with support and guidance associated with fraud incidents and any reported unusual/suspicious activity.
  • Provide guidance to customer victims on the appropriate course of action and provide fraud prevention counseling as needed (i.e., ID Theft, wire fraud, malware, phishing)
  • Remain current with arising fraud trends and activities by attending networking workshops and/or training.
  • May prepare security alerts/bulletins for internal dissemination.
  • May travel to off-site locations for investigative purposes.
  • Prioritize tasks to ensure deadlines and expectations are met.
  • Work cases with a sense of urgency while ensuring the accuracy of information.
  • Maintain confidentiality surrounding fraud methods and investigations.
  • Build effective relationships with internal/external stakeholders (e.g., law enforcement agencies and other Financial Institutions to collaborate in investigations).
  • Network and develop effective contacts in the private, public and government sector, to assist in fraud investigations.

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's Degree Criminal Justice preferred.
  • Three (3) to Five (5) years in fraud investigations or law enforcement capacity required.
  • Strong understanding of financial transactions required.
  • Conducts interviews of witnesses and suspects as required by the investigations.
  • Working knowledge of bank products, services, bank systems and transaction types preferred

title: Journeyperson / Columbus
description:
SCOPE OF WORK
Ability to lead and perform installations, alterations, additions, and/or repairs of electrical systems, conductors, and associated materials and equipment within the residential, commercial, and industrial electrical industry.
Proficient in troubleshooting and proactively problem-solving electrical systems.
POSITION REQUIREMENTS

Uses Gaylor Values as tools to carry out all job responsibilities
Understands and complies with Company and job safety requirements (O.S.H.A.)
Understands and follows lock out tag out procedures
Acquires and maintains personal hand tools per Company policy
Certified to operate platform and boom lifts, or able to obtain certification upon hire
Able to perform work at various heights, up to 90’, from ladders, scaffolds, aerial lifts, cat walks, roofs, or other designated safe work areas
Works from all assigned types of mobile elevated work platforms
Able to accurately bend and install all types of conduit

Understands use of degrees in bending conduit (i.e. concentric bending)

Able to use two handed tools/equipment (i.e. cable cutters, hammer drills, compression tools, jack hammers, etc.)
Understands and has ability to properly erect pulley systems to lift/move heavy equipment
Possesses knowledge of and ability to properly give “hand signals” to operators
Understands various types of switching of branch circuits (i.e. 3-way, 4-way, etc.)
Possesses knowledge of circuit grounding practices, transformer connections, over-current protection, parallel circuits, fuse/circuit breakers, motors, cable trays and their supports
Possesses knowledge of effects of soil on underground installations and cables
Possesses knowledge of trench safety required during installation of underground conductors

Possesses knowledge of other trades, including concrete, masonry, metals, and wood construction methods
Possesses skill to accurately plan and install conductors in conduits and raceways
Possesses knowledge of and ability to accurately install electrical devices and fixtures in a timely manner
Able to work in restrictive/tight areas (i.e. switchgear rooms, crawl spaces, utility tunnels, attics, etc.)
Able to install switchgear and perform the required terminations
Has experience in terminations/splicing up to and including 600 volts
Possesses technical knowledge, safety knowledge, and ability to work with live and energized parts
Leads and assists in all types of wire pulls (i.e. conduit, cable tray, floor ducts, wire way, etc.)
Understands verbal instructions and heeds safety warnings
Demonstrates and exhibits proper use and safe handling of tools, equipment, and materials
Reads and understands labels, job site maps/directions, instruction manuals, and written instructions
Possesses knowledge of blueprints, shop drawings, ladder logic diagrams, and has ability to visualize completed work prior to installation

Understands and complies with NEC, state, and local codes

Understand basic math and can properly read tape measure

Able to add, subtract, divide, multiply, and accurately use electrical formulas

Takes pride in craftsmanship

RESPONSIBILITIES

Reports to assigned job site location on time, as directed
Maintains and properly stores tools, materials, and equipment
Organizes materials and tools to maintain clean and neat work area
Possesses ability to dig trenches, either by use of hand tools or equipment as necessary
Mounts and installs assigned hardware (such as conduit, wires, and strapping) as directed
Accurately identifies colors of wires and conductors
Plans, schedules, and organizes tasks to meet deadlines
Accurately interprets electrical construction drawings, terminates cables, installs, and trouble shoots control wiring from schematics
Completes routine daily inspections of equipment and work areas to verify accurate and timely installations
Completes and documents regular safety inspections, as assigned
Accurately and effectively directs and trains Helpers and Apprentices in proper work practices to meet production requirements
Safely performs assigned tasks with limited supervision

WORKING CONDITIONS

May require working in all elements (heat, cold, rain, snow, etc.) depending on job location and/or time of year

Must be able to utilize construction site sanitary facilities (port-o-lets)
Must have required hand tools at all times while at work site (waist tool belts can weigh up to 30 lbs.)
Must be able to work scheduled hours as well as overtime, as required, on short notice
Must be able to work in noisy environments
Must be able to remain calm in times of heightened emotional situations
Must work well with others as a member of a team to complete tasks

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Must be able to wear personnel protective equipment (i.e., hard hat, safety glasses, gloves, high visibility vest, safety harness, etc.) when required
Ability to stand, bend, stoop, squat, crawl, climb, kneel, balance, push, pull, and reach overhead for extended periods of time
Ability to lift loads of up to 51 lbs.
Repetitive use of arms, hands, and fingers
Ability to climb and use ladders and scaffolding of all types for extended periods of time
Possess good vision/hearing (normal or corrected)
Ability to make transition from designated employee parking areas to construction areas and be able to gain access to all levels of building/structure, even if only means of access is by OSHA approved site construction ladder or stairs still under construction but deemed safe for use
Ability to work while constantly moving
Ability to reach and stretch to position equipment, fixtures, etc. while maintaining balance
Ability to use both hands simultaneously for tying knots and for proper use of power equipment
Must be able to see color to discern color-coded wiring
Must be physically capable of pulling wires and cables through conduits

EDUCATION

High School graduate or equivalency, preferred

EXPERIENCE

Accredited Apprenticeship Program completion or six years on the job electrical experience required
Journeyman License requirement in states, locales, or projects, as required

title: Construction Superintendent
description:
Construction Superintendent

Benderson Development is one of America’s largest privately held real estate companies, with a portfolio that includes more than 1,000 properties totaling over 50 million square feet in 40 states. The diverse Benderson portfolio includes retail, office, industrial, hotel, residential, and landholdings. With over 75 years of experience, Benderson Development has engineered impressive growth through innovation, insight, and determination.

Summary

The Construction Superintendent will be accountable for the entire construction project from mobilization to completion, by providing the knowledge, skill, and experience to run day-to-day operations on the job site. This includes field coordination, working closely with the Subcontractors to ensure that quality and workmanship meets Benderson standards. The Superintendent will ensure that the work is carried out safely, correctly, within budget, and on schedule.

Principle Responsibilities & Duties

  • Plan, coordinate, and direct efficient use of all labor, equipment, materials, subcontractors/ material suppliers to achieve the highest quality.
  • Study contract drawings and specifications in detail. Check all dimensions and bring all discrepancies and omissions to the attention of designers and Project Managers.
  • Assist management in the selection of contractors for the right job at the right price.
  • Monitor progress of construction and review schedule status with Project Manager weekly.
  • Inspect subcontractor work to verify quality and conformance to the construction documents. Review the construction drawings, documents, and contract scopes of work.
  • Review, approve and/or dispute T&M sheets daily, as they are turned in by the subcontractors.
  • Meet utility company reps on-site to coordinate utility services.
  • Expedite material and equipment orders in a timely fashion to ensure “just in time inventory"
  • Evaluate the effectiveness and evaluate the performance of field personnel/ subcontractors and their crews.
  • Coordinate construction activities with tenant representatives to minimize the impact on their operations while obtaining a high degree of construction efficiency
  • Coordinate Tenant Openings with Property Management.
  • Obtain a Certificate of Occupancy and/or Certificate of Compliance for each project.
  • Promote and ensure job site safety

Qualifications

  • Must have an active driver's license.
  • Minimum of 5 years experience in the construction industry as a Superintendent.
  • Commercial, new construction experience required; Retail construction experience highly preferred.
  • Must be willing to drive to job sites within a 1-3 hour radius of Sarasota.
  • Highly motivated, with a demonstrated passion for excellence and taking initiative.
  • Professional with the ability to effectively communicate with all levels of the organization.

Physical Requirements

  • Normal dexterity required in construction and office environment including hand-eye coordination, walking, sitting, standing, alertness (attention to detail), computer input, and answering of phones.
  • May require lifting of materials or boxes weighing up to 50 pounds.
  • Much sitting and driving for extended periods of time to get to locations, and walking to perform an inspection of locations

title: Staff Construction Observer
description:
The Construction Observer provides full-time, on-site observation and documentation of construction activities to assist the Client in monitoring project progress and the general conformance of the work with project plans, specifications, and contract documents. The Construction Observer serves as an independent observer and reporter, documenting construction activities, identifying apparent deficiencies, and communicating observations to the Client's designated representatives. The role does not include construction management, contractor supervision, safety management, or acceptance of the work.

The position required full-time travel Monday-Friday.

  • Maintain a daily on-site presence during active construction operations as directed by the Client.
  • Observe and document construction activities for general conformance with project drawings, specifications, and contract requirements.
  • Monitor installation activities associated with building systems and components, including architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and fire protection work.
  • Prepare detailed daily field reports documenting workforce activity, work progress, observed conditions, weather impacts, site logistics, and noteworthy project events.
  • Communicate observed deficiencies, nonconforming work, or potential concerns to the Client's Site Superintendent and designated representatives in a timely manner.
  • Maintain accurate photographic and written records of construction progress and significant project milestones.
  • Attend required project meetings, site orientations, and safety briefings as directed by the Client.
  • Coordinate daily activities through the Client's designated site representative.
  • Track project progress and maintain organized documentation to support project reporting and historical records.
  • Notify the Client of observed jobsite safety concerns while recognizing that enforcement of safety requirements remains the responsibility of the Contractor.
  • Bachelor’s degree in building science or related building field and 5-7 years’ experience in facility assessment, construction observation, construction inspection, field engineering, superintendent, or related construction experience. Or, in lieu of a degree, 9-11 years’ related experience.
  • A valid driver’s license with acceptable violation history may be required.
  • Strong understanding of commercial building construction methods, sequencing, and construction documentation.
  • Ability to read and interpret drawings, specifications, submittals, and contract documents.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and digital reporting platforms.
  • Strong written communication and documentation skills.
  • Ability to work independently with limited supervision while maintaining professional interactions with project stakeholders.

title: INTERNATIONAL LOGISTICS COORDINATOR
description:
Purpose of the job
Reporting to the International Division, you play a key role in coordinating, tracking and optimizing shipments to our international licensed partners. You ensure that every shipment, from origin to final destination, is executed with accuracy, efficiency and full compliance, while respecting operational standards, local requirements and applicable regulations. Through your strong organizational skills and proactive approach, you directly contribute to the efficiency of our international operations and to delivering a seamless partner experience.

Key Responsibilities

Coordinate and monitor international shipments transiting through our overseas 3PL warehouses to ensure on time delivery, while meeting operational requirements and market specific needs;
Plan and coordinate exports from Montreal, including the transmission of export data to Canadian customs authorities through required systems;
Follow up daily with suppliers regarding purchase order booking requests for international licensed partners;
Collaborate closely with freight forwarders to review, validate and optimize shipment bookings;
Ensure compliance of all shipments, including cross trade and direct exports, with applicable regulations, policies and procedures;
Prepare, validate and coordinate all required commercial documentation for customs clearance and ensure timely transmission to all stakeholders;
Issue and send invoices to licensed partners according to established terms and follow up as needed;
Build and maintain strong business relationships with international licensed partners by providing a professional and solution oriented service;
Act as a key point of contact with external partners involved in shipments, including freight forwarders, carriers and other stakeholders;
Ensure clear and fluid communication with internal teams to maintain up-to-date visibility on the status of merchandise and non-merchandise shipments;
Update and maintain accurate shipment information to ensure reliable tracking and partner visibility;
Identify opportunities for continuous improvement and recommend practical solutions to optimize logistics processes;
Analyze logistics performance indicators such as transit times and delivery performance and share insights with stakeholders;
Support the international logistics team with various projects and related tasks as needed;

Your profile

Versatility and curiosity: You are always eager to explore new ways of working and adapt to diverse realities within international markets. You enjoy learning and understanding the complexities of global logistics.
Organization and prioritization: You are able to manage multiple files at once while maintaining a clear overall perspective. Even in a fast paced environment, you remain structured, efficient and results oriented.
Collaboration and communication: You communicate with ease in both written and spoken French and English. You easily build trusting relationships with your colleagues and partners, both internal and external.
Attention to detail: You are recognized for your precision and strong attention to detail. You ensure that every step is properly executed and that nothing is overlooked.

College diploma (or equivalent) in transportation and logistics
Minimum of 5 years of related experience
Fluency in French and English, both spoken and written. (The candidate must be able to communicate with people outside Quebec)
Excellent communication skills; able to build and maintain effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders

title: Dock Worker
description:
About the Role:

The Dock Worker plays a crucial role in the logistics and supply chain process, ensuring that parts are efficiently loaded and unloaded from trucks and delivery vehicles. This position is responsible for maintaining the flow of parts in and out of the warehouse, which directly impacts the company's ability to meet customer demands. The Dock Worker will work closely with team members to ensure that all shipments are accurately processed, safely packaged to prevent damage, and that inventory levels are maintained. Attention to detail and adherence to safety protocols are essential to prevent accidents and ensure the integrity of the parts being handled. Ultimately, the Dock Worker contributes to the overall success of the organization by facilitating timely deliveries and maintaining high standards of operational efficiency.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Ability to lift heavy objects (up to 50 lbs) and perform physical tasks.
  • Basic understanding of shipping and receiving processes.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Previous experience in a shipping or warehouse environment.
  • Forklift certification or experience operating material handling equipment.
  • Knowledge of inventory management systems.

Responsibilities:

  • Load and unload parts from trucks and delivery vehicles, sometimes utilizing forklifts and other equipment.
  • Packaging parts with appropriate materials or in appropriate format on trucks to prevent damage.
  • Inspect parts/loads for accuracy and damage, reporting any discrepancies.
  • Organize and maintain the shipping dock area to ensure a safe and efficient working environment.
  • Collaborate with warehouse staff to ensure timely processing of orders and inventory management.
  • Adhere to safety regulations and company policies while performing all tasks.

Skills:

The required skills for this position include physical stamina and the ability to work in a fast-paced environment, which are essential for loading and unloading shipments efficiently. Attention to detail is critical, as the Dock Worker must accurately inspect shipments and maintain inventory records. Communication skills are also important, as the worker will need to collaborate with team members and report any issues that arise. Preferred skills, such as forklift operation, enhance the worker's ability to move heavy items safely and efficiently. Overall, a combination of physical and organizational skills will ensure that the Dock Worker contributes effectively to the logistics process.

title: Spring 2027 Co-op, Asset Management
description:
About the role:


The Asset Management Co‑op will help support the day‑to‑day operational and technical performance of BlueWave’s operating solar and storage assets. This Spring 2027 Co‑op (January-June) is designed for students currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program and based in the Boston area. This role provides hands‑on exposure to asset operations, project onboarding, data analysis, and cross‑functional collaboration. It is especially well‑suited for students interested in renewable energy, engineering, operations, or data analytics.


Please note that this is a 6‑month Co‑op position running from January through June 2027. The role follows a hybrid schedule, with Co‑op students expected to work Monday through Friday and commute into BlueWave’s Boston office at least 3 days per week.


What you'll do:


Support Asset Operations & Monitoring

  • Monitor solar and storage asset performance using SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition), a centralized platform that allows operators to remotely track and manage the performance of power generation assets, along with asset management systems.

Asset Registry & Technical Documentation

Cross‑Functional Collaboration

Research & Reporting

Qualifications:

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
Senior Data Engineer - Data Engineering

Barbican & Epsom | Hybrid Working (1 office day per week) | Permanent | Full-Time

Competitive salary available, depending on experience

37.5 hours per week


At Nuffield Health, everything we give our patients, members and customers starts with our people. Your passion, your expertise and your drive to make a difference enable us to deliver exceptional connected healthcare and fitness experiences.


We're looking for an experienced Senior Data Engineer to join our Data Engineering team, responsible for making data available and trusted across the whole of Nuffield Health. This is a role with real ownership: you'll own a functional area of our data platform, lead delivery initiatives and line manage engineers, setting the standards, patterns and direction that the wider team follows.


Our Data Engineering team operates a distributed leadership model. Each Senior Data Engineer owns a defined functional area, such as ingestion and integration, incident management and observability, governance, security and cost management, or CI/CD and DevOps, and is accountable for the standards and resilience of that area so that nothing depends on a single person. Seniors lead delivery initiatives and line manage engineers, with the Lead Data Engineer retaining overall technical direction and the roadmap. You'll work with industry-leading technologies including Snowflake, dbt, Azure Data Factory, Talend, SQL Server, New Relic and Terraform.

Could you play a key role in that?


As our Senior Data Engineer, you'll:


  • Own a defined functional area of the data platform, setting the standards, patterns and tooling the team follows within it and acting as the first point of contact for questions in that area.
  • Avoid becoming a single point of dependency by documenting your work and helping other engineers develop the knowledge and skills needed to support your area, treating knowledge transfer as an ongoing obligation rather than a one-off handover.
  • Lead delivery initiatives end to end, planning, resourcing and delivering against agreed constraints in collaboration with Product Owners, Delivery Managers, architects and third-party suppliers.
  • Line manage engineers, including objectives, development plans and reviews, and line manage external or temporary resource aligned to your initiatives for their duration.
  • Design, build and operate robust ingestion, integration and transformation solutions on Snowflake, dbt and Azure, in line with Nuffield Health's enterprise architecture and data engineering standards.
  • Ensure solutions are operationally ready, observable and supportable, and contribute to incident and problem management as part of the team's service management approach.
  • Coach mid-level engineers to take ownership of epics and smaller initiatives within their squad, growing the next generation of leaders in the team.
  • Contribute to the team's technical roadmap, BAU planning and engineering maturity, including documentation, code quality, branching and testing standards.
  • Escalate cross-cutting risks, dependencies and unassigned questions to the Lead Data Engineer, and communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

To succeed as Senior Data Engineer, you'll bring:


  • Substantial hands-on data engineering experience across integration, data modelling and data warehousing, with excellent SQL skills.
  • Experience with ETL/ELT tools (e.g. Talend, Azure Data Factory, dbt) and database platforms (e.g. MS SQL Server, Snowflake, Azure SQL Database), including developing integration solutions using APIs, files and databases.
  • Experience with performance tuning, data migration strategies (on premise and cloud) and relational database design, particularly in support of business intelligence.
  • Experience setting and upholding engineering standards, and taking ownership of quality and outcomes for a technical area.
  • Experience leading the delivery of a project or initiative, working with Product Owners, Delivery Managers, architects and third-party suppliers to manage scope, dependencies and risk.
  • Line management or mentoring experience, or a clear appetite to develop it with structured support.
  • Excellent communication skills, including documenting technical design proposals and translating complex technical concepts for technical and non-technical audiences.

Desirable:


  • Observability and incident management tooling, such as New Relic and ServiceNow.
  • CI/CD, DevOps and infrastructure as code, such as Terraform and Azure DevOps.
  • Data governance and security: data masking, GDPR, access auditing, PII handling, role-based access and cloud cost management.
  • Experience in healthcare or another regulated environment.

We will provide:


  • A wide variety of interesting and challenging work that involves most of Nuffield Health's systems, working with key stakeholders such as data analysts, data scientists and business intelligence teams.
  • Genuine ownership of a functional area and the initiatives you lead, within a community of data engineers where your opinions shape the standards and practices we adopt.
  • A structured path into technical leadership and people management: training pathways, shadowing and reverse shadowing, a Seniors peer group, and regular reviews with the Lead Data Engineer.
  • Opportunities to learn and develop your career through apprenticeships, self-learning, mentoring and training courses, with progression encouraged both within the team and across Nuffield Health.
  • An environment that allows you to perform at your best, working collaboratively with colleagues who are focused on improving the health of our nation and making a real difference to people's everyday lives.

Helping you feel good.


We want you to love coming to work, feeling healthy, happy and valued. That’s why we’ve developed a benefits package with you in mind. Here, you can choose from a range of fitness, lifestyle, health and fitness wellbeing rewards, such as free gym membership, health assessments, retail discounts and pension options.


At Nuffield Health, we take care of what’s important to you.

title: Graduate Assistant Surveyor (Cost Management) - US Based
description:
Position Category: Graduate
Location: G&T's US team is currently recruiting for opportunities across the following locations: New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Miami.
Start Date: September 2027
Eligibility Requirement: Please note that only candidates who have previously completed, or are currently studying, a degree accredited by the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS) are eligible for this role.

Summary
The role of a cost manager is to manage the cost and legal processes of a construction project. As a Cost Manager, your primary responsibility is to help ensure projects are delivered within the client's approved budget.

This includes preparing cost plans, forecasts, cash flow projections, contract documentation and financial reports, while providing clients with clear and accurate advice throughout the project lifecycle. Effective communication and strong attention to detail are key to the role, enabling Cost Managers to keep clients informed of project finances and proactively manage associated risks.

Role Overview
As an Assistant Surveyor within one of G&T's US offices, you will gain valuable practical experience across a variety of projects while developing a comprehensive understanding of construction costs, procurement and contracts.

Working alongside experienced Cost Managers, you will receive on-the-job training and support to help develop the technical, commercial and professional skills required to build a successful career in the industry. You will also be encouraged and supported in working towards Chartered Membership of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS) through the APC pathway.

The role offers exposure to a range of clients, sectors and project types, providing an excellent opportunity to apply the knowledge gained through your degree in a practical project environment while continuing your professional development.

Working as part of a collaborative team, you will support your line manager and colleagues in the delivery of project work. You will be expected to take ownership of tasks, work with an appropriate level of autonomy and recognise when to seek guidance to achieve the best outcomes for clients and projects.

We are particularly interested in candidates who are enthusiastic about developing their careers within the US construction and property industry and who are excited by the opportunity to contribute to the continued growth of G&T's US business.

You will build a strong understanding of your role, the firm, the US market and the wider industry, and how they all connect to deliver successful projects.
Working with your line manager the role will typically include the following:
  • Measuring drawings provided by the design team, either manually or using measurement software such as CostX.
  • Using measurements and an understanding of construction methods to prepare cost plans that establish project budgets for clients.
  • Compiling contract documentation, including drawing registers, preliminaries and pricing documents for tendering purposes.
  • Receiving tender submissions and preparing tender analysis reports and clarification schedules for contractor responses.
  • Reviewing and comparing tender returns to support recommendations on contractor appointments.
  • Preparing cash flow forecasts for clients.
  • Attending site visits and undertaking valuations of completed works, producing the required analysis and documentation to facilitate payment in accordance with contract requirements.
  • Supporting value engineering exercises to identify opportunities for cost savings and improved value.
  • Attending project meetings and site meetings, including design team meetings and contractor progress meetings, depending on the project stage.
  • Communicating with a range of stakeholders, including suppliers, contractors, design teams and clients, and providing support on cost-related matters and project variations.
  • Achieved or expected to achieve a 2:1 or above in a RICS accredited degree.
  • Excellent working knowledge of current IT systems.
  • Strong understanding of the importance of client care and relationship building.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Trustworthy, reliable and professional in approach.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise workload effectively.
  • Ability to work efficiently and deliver to deadlines.
  • Comfortable working both independently and as part of a collaborative team.
  • Proactive, adaptable and flexible when responding to different situations.
  • Demonstrates dedication, commitment and a positive attitude.
  • Eagerness to learn and continually develop professionally.
  • Genuine interest in the construction and property industry.
  • Enthusiasm for developing a career in the US construction and property industry, with a desire to build market knowledge and professional experience within the US sector.

title: Senior Program Manager
description:
Take ownership. Challenge assumptions. Deliver precise, measurable results.

You dig into complex problems, question answers that lack evidence, and take initiative when you see a better way forward. You are comfortable making decisions, speaking directly, and tackling difficult conversations. You move with urgency—and hold yourself accountable for getting the details right.

At Willdan, these strengths can help shape the performance of energy efficiency programs and the teams that deliver them.

We are seeking a Senior Program Manager to lead new construction energy efficiency programs with operating budgets of $2 million or more. You will combine technical knowledge, independent judgment, and disciplined execution to achieve program goals, strengthen client relationships, and improve how work gets done.

How you approach the work

You think independently and look beyond today’s process to what could work better. You assess risks, develop a sound recommendation, and take ownership of moving it forward. When an assumption, decision, or approach needs to be challenged, you address it directly and respectfully, using facts to support your position.

You enjoy examining technical information and working through problems that require focused thought. You can work independently, investigate competing explanations, and distinguish evidence from opinion. You communicate conclusions clearly, explain your reasoning, and remain willing to revise your position when the facts warrant it.

You bring a natural sense of urgency to your work. You can manage varied responsibilities, respond to shifting priorities, and make timely decisions under pressure. When progress stalls, you identify the obstacle and take action.

You also recognize that speed requires discipline. You check critical details, follow applicable policies and contractual requirements, and see commitments through to completion. You know when an established process must be followed and when to propose a change through the appropriate channels.

What you will own

  • Program direction and results. Set priorities across multiple programs, anticipate challenges, and translate annual objectives into clear plans. Monitor performance and make timely adjustments to meet commitments.
  • Technical and operational problem-solving. Examine data, question assumptions, identify underlying causes, and develop practical solutions to complex program issues.
  • Budgets and resources. Define staffing and budget requirements, collaborate with the financial manager on forecasts, and make informed decisions about resource allocation.
  • Quality and compliance. Direct internal and external resources to meet utility requirements, contract goals, budgets, and cost-effectiveness expectations. Maintain accurate reporting and thorough follow-through.
  • Process improvement. Identify inefficient practices and lead improvements to tools, procedures, and workflows for staff, subcontractors, and trade allies. Evaluate the risks and benefits of proposed changes.
  • Client relationships. Build credibility through preparation, technical understanding, and dependable delivery. Address concerns promptly, navigate difficult conversations, and communicate issues and recommendations candidly.
  • Team leadership. Establish clear expectations, delegate meaningful responsibility, and hold people accountable. Mentor program management staff and help them develop sound judgment and greater independence.
  • Reporting and communication. Prepare quarterly and annual business reviews that clearly explain performance, risks, and recommended actions. Adapt technical information to the needs of clients, leadership, and program teams.
  • Program continuity. Support senior leadership and business development in contract negotiations and continuations with factual analysis and a clear understanding of delivery requirements.

What you bring

  • In-depth knowledge of energy efficiency technologies, industry standards, and regulatory frameworks, supported by an understanding of building science, construction, and sustainability.
  • Demonstrated experience in strategic planning, program or project management, and execution against measurable goals.
  • Strong analytical judgment and the confidence to make decisions, explain tradeoffs, and take responsibility for outcomes.
  • Proven ability to lead and mentor a team, coordinate resources, and address performance issues directly and professionally.
  • The discipline to manage competing deadlines while maintaining accuracy, documentation, and compliance.
  • Clear, factual written and verbal communication, including reports, presentations, recommendations, and client discussions.
  • Experience coordinating promotional activities relevant to the industry.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
  • A bachelor’s or master’s degree in architecture, mechanical or electrical engineering, construction management, building science, communications, business, or a closely related field—or equivalent experience.
