title: Principal Data Scientist (AI-assisted Clinical Development)
description:
A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Roche.

This role is based in the Innovation Accelerator (IA) team, the innovation engine and connective tissue for Design, Data and Data Science innovation strategy within Product Development Data Sciences (PDD). We translate our long-term PDD vision into actionable strategy, shaping and prioritizing innovative cross-functional use cases that span PDD, PD, and Pharma. As both integrators and incubators, we explore, prototype, and help productize solutions to deliver impact in close partnership with internal Roche teams and external collaborators. With a mindset rooted in openness, value creation, and adaptability, we navigate the innovation ecosystem to drive transformative impact and future readiness across the organization.

**The Opportunity:**

The IA **Principal****Data Scientist**plays a pivotal role in building and deploying AI/ML-powered digital solutions that transform how we develop medicines. You will partner closely with product managers, software engineers, and UX researchers to design, test, and scale statistical capabilities that unlock actionable insights from clinical, operational, and real-world data. With a strong product-thinking mindset and deep technical fluency, you will help create intelligent tools that are scalable, ethical, and built for impact in regulated healthcare environments.

- You support or lead the development and application of advanced statistical and machine learning methods for integration into tools and software products in clinical development and decision-making support

- You design and productize the execution of simulation studies to evaluate innovative trial designs and statistical frameworks

- You translate complex scientific and operational considerations into software requirements that productize model development and usage, collaborating with domain experts to productize the validation of assumptions and result interpretation

- You independently drive exploratory analysis of complex clinical, biomarker, and operational data to extract insights and develop predictive models

- You develop scalable, reproducible pipelines for data processing, model training, evaluation, and deployment in regulated environments

- You optimize model performance, ensure algorithmic fairness, proactively mitigate bias or drift in deployed systems, and develop evaluation approaches for algorithms including generative AI (GenAI) components

- You co-lead the architectural design of ML and GenAI systems supporting traceability, compliance, and explainability

- You partner with software engineering, product, UX, and science teams to integrate models into real-world user applications

- You contribute to scientific leadership by publishing and presenting novel methodologies in high-impact venues, both internal and external

- You serve as a best-practice resource for statistical modeling strategies, code quality, and responsible AI principles

- You lead or co-lead cross-functional data science efforts that impact portfolio strategy and delivery


**Who you are:**

- You have a Master’s or PhD in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Bioinformatics, or a related field

- You have 6+ years of experience applying advanced statistical and ML techniques in biomedical, clinical, or digital health domains

- You have proven expertise in model development, simulation studies, and decision-support frameworks

- You have strong hands-on experience with Python or R, and ML libraries such as scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch, or similar

- You have a track record of translating complex domain questions into robust statistical models or ML systems

- You have experience building pipelines for training, evaluating, and deploying ML solutions in production environments

- You have demonstrated expertise with RWD, Bayesian methods, decision theory, high-dimensional data, or causal inference

- You have attention to detail and quality work with an ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects simultaneously, including both long-term and short-term initiatives

- You have excellent collaboration skills, including statistical consulting skills, interpersonal skills to contribute effectively in cross-functional team settings, ability to influence others without authority, and ability to build strong collaborative relationships with scientific and non-scientific partners

- You have capacity for independent thinking and ability to make decisions based upon sound principles

- You exhibit excellent strategic agility including problem-solving and critical thinking skills, and agility that extends beyond technical domain

- You demonstrate respect for cultural differences when interacting with colleagues in the global workplace

- You possess excellent verbal and written communication skills, specifically in the areas of presentation and writing, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts in clear language


**Preferred:**

- Experience leading technical design or mentoring junior team members

- Experience applying Agile software development practices, ideally for a product embedding statistical algorithms and/or GenAI

- Experience prototyping and launching innovative data science or AI products

- Experience deploying ML models in compliant, regulated environments

- Experience developing evidence synthesis models or methods (e.g., network meta-analysis) and/or approaches to construct data-driven priors for drug development

- Experience with Bayesian computing or probabilistic programming languages (PPLs), including Stan, PyMC, brms, or others

- Experience with AI-native software engineering practices

- Familiarity with data governance, privacy, and regulatory frameworks relevant to ML in pharma

- Exposure to multiple stages of the pharma development life cycle (e.g., early development, assessment of external molecules for business development, commercialization)

- Familiarity with cloud-native ML architectures, ML Ops tools, or real-world data pipelines

- Strong publication record or external visibility in scientific communities


**Location**

- This position is based in Boston, MA

- Relocation assistance is not available

title: Dassault Falcon 900B Captain/ARM
description:
WHO YOU’RE EVALUATING:
Wonder what it's like flying for the most pilot-friendly
aircraft management company?
Silver Air prides operating with a culture of excellence, and
pilots are at the core of the vision. You’ll join a team that knows how to
provide the highest quality experience to our team members and clients. We have
the highest-rated independent auditing firm certifications in private jetting.
Your experience is our most important asset, so we work hard to
create an environment that keeps you thriving. We designed your benefits
package (below) with a pilot’s needs in mind.


WHO YOU ARE:
As a Lead Captain, you’re responsible for operating the aircraft
in a safe and sensible manner. You're a pilot who hones their aviation skills
daily and cooperates with the crew easily. To do that, you should:

  1. Communicate professionally with crew members and clients at all times. You adapt well to different people and can adjust your working
    style.
  2. Thrive in changing environments and have the flexibility for priorities that switch instantly. You'll be in a fast-paced environment while on call.
  3. Ambitiously work on being the best pilot you can be. Your coworkers want to do that, too, so you'll fit right in.

WHAT YOU’LL LEAD:
You're responsible for the safe and efficient conduct of the
flight as the Lead Captain. Your duties include:

  • Ensure the safety of all passengers, aircraft, and crew
  • Reviewing the maintenance status
  • Conducting proper pre-flight inspections
  • Following all policies according to Silver Air and applicable Federal Aviation Regulations
  • Plan and execute flight operations for private jets, including flight planning, fuel management, and weight and balance calculations
  • The conduct of a proper pre-flight inspection in accordance with the approved Aircraft Flight Manual
  • A complete check of weather and facilities along the route to be flown and airports to be used, including alternate airports
Accurate completion of all trip paperwork in accordance with current procedures.


WHAT IS AN ARM? (AVIATION RESOURCE MANAGEMENT):
  • Liaison with the Aircraft Owner and the internal Silver Air departments to ensure the aircraft
    is operated efficiently and according to the overall management plan
  • Be a LEADER and MENTOR to all team members assigned to the aircraft
  • Understand the management plan of the aircraft, including the Owner’s personal use and charter levels set forth in the management agreement with the Aircraft Owner, and ensure goals are being met
  • Collaborate with the dedicated Maintenance Manager to coordinate and oversee schedule and unscheduled maintenance events
  • Ensure the aircraft is stocked and mission ready for all Owner and charter flights
  • Partner with People and Culture regarding all crewing activities, including developing a crew plan, communicating with owners, applicants, and Chief Pilot
  • Be involved in scheduling of flight crew for charters and owner flights and work with Flight Support to establish a Hard Days Off schedule with all flight crew team members
  • Ensure the efficient and cost-effective use of both internal and external resources for the aircraft
  • Provide training and guidance to personnel on ARM best practices and procedures
  • Review the monthly statement items with the dedicated Accounting Manager and the dedicated Maintenance Manager
WHAT YOU BRING:
You have the experience to transition over to Silver Air with
ease.

  • Total time in all aircraft = 3500 hours/3000 hours as PIC.
  • Multi-engine time = 3000 hours/2000 hours as PIC.
  • Total Turbine time = 1750 hours preferred.
  • Total time in airplane type = 200 hours/100 hours as PIC.
  • Type rated on DA-50. Or comparable aircraft.
  • Valid First Class Medical Certificate. This is required.
  • Previous Part 135 experience. This is preferred, but not required.
  • Compliant with ICAO Annex I - 2.1.1.0. As it pertains to aircraft engaged in
    international commercial air transport operations with more than one pilot.
  • CANPASS authorization. You'll need the ability to obtain and maintain CANPASS authorization for unrestricted travel to/from Canada as a commercial pilot.

WHO YOU’LL BE WORKING WITH:
We don’t believe in floating fleets, so you’ll work with the same
three pilots for the specific tail number and aircraft type.
Your teams consist of a Lead Captain, Captain, and First Officer.
You’ll also be supported by a Flight Management and Support team.
Your success depends on how the rest of the team supports you. You'll see we strive to make Silver Air an incredible place to work for pilots.
The specific benefits / perks we offer are continually evolving, but currently include:
  • Personalized schedule with 10 days off per month and 20 days scheduled for flight.
  • Our Flight Support team handles travel logistics.
  • Paid leadership, hospitality, and flight simulator training with a one-year training agreement.
  • Fly well-maintained equipment with modern technology.
  • KCM badge, paid medical exams, extra passports, and cell phone stipend.
  • Premium medical benefits fully paid for employee and family, vision, dental, life insurance, HSA, and FSA.
  • 5% company match on 401(k) from day one.
  • Employee Assistance Program for personal concerns.
  • Competitive compensation with regular pay reviews.

title: Drilling Solutions Engineer
description:
About the Opportunity
Altitude Energy Partners is seeking a Drilling Solutions Engineer to support technical drilling performance, optimization, and execution across drilling services operations. This role works closely with Operations, Field, Sales, Engineering, and customer personnel to develop and implement drilling solutions that improve performance, efficiency, reliability, and overall well execution.
The successful candidate will analyze historical and real-time drilling data, drilling dynamics, and well objectives to optimize drilling parameters, BHA and equipment selection, directional drilling performance, and post-job results. This position provides technical support and recommendations throughout pre-job planning, execution, troubleshooting, customer engagement, and continuous improvement activities.

Key Responsibilities

Analyze historical and real-time drilling data to identify drilling trends, dysfunction, performance gaps, and opportunities for optimization.
Use drilling analysis tools, parameter comparisons, and torque and drag modelling where applicable to evaluate performance and provide technical recommendations.
Monitor drilling parameters and recommend adjustments to improve drilling efficiency, directional performance, and downhole tool performance.
Support equipment selection and optimization, including bit, BHA, motor, and downhole tool combinations based on well objectives, formation characteristics, ROP, durability, and application requirements.
Assist with directional drilling planning and execution, including well plans, survey requirements, BHA performance, and drilling parameter optimization.
Provide technical support to Operations and field personnel during job execution and troubleshoot drilling or downhole tool performance issues.
Review well objectives, offset performance, equipment selection, BHA configuration, drilling parameters, and operational risks during pre-job planning.
Conduct post-job performance analysis to evaluate drilling results, service quality, equipment performance, and opportunities for improvement.
Participate in failure investigations and root cause analysis, providing technical input on operational, application, and equipment-related factors.
Identify service quality and performance trends and recommend improvements to Operations, Engineering, Repair and Maintenance, and management.

Develop strong working relationships with customer office personnel, field supervision, rig personnel, and other key stakeholders.
Work directly with customers to understand drilling objectives and provide technical recommendations based on operational requirements and performance data.
Support customer meetings, presentations, performance reviews, and incident analysis as required.
Provide feedback to internal and external engineering groups on field performance, tool functionality, reliability, testing requirements, and product improvement opportunities.
Assist with the development and standardization of drilling performance reports, KPIs, well summaries, and other technical deliverables.
Coach and support field and customer personnel in drilling performance monitoring, optimization techniques, and best practices.
Maintain current knowledge of drilling technologies, downhole tools, industry practices, customer requirements, and market developments.
Support Sales and Business Development with technical information and presentations as needed.
Perform other duties as assigned by management.

Education and Experience

High School Diploma or equivalent is required.
Technical degree, certification, or degree in an Engineering discipline is preferred.
Minimum of five years of experience in drilling engineering, directional drilling, drill-site operations, drilling optimization, or a related oil and gas service role.
Experience supporting drilling operations and analyzing drilling performance data is preferred.

Skills and Qualifications

Extensive knowledge of downhole drilling tools and directional drilling operations.
Strong understanding of the well construction process, including directional drilling and M/LWD operations.
Knowledge of drilling dynamics, drilling dysfunction identification, drilling parameter optimization, and performance analysis.
Ability to understand and recommend conventional BHA configurations used to hold, build, or drop inclination based on drilling requirements.
Understanding of directional well planning, survey management, dogleg severity, build rate, walk rate, magnetic declination, and grid declination.
Ability to analyze drilling data and translate findings into practical operational recommendations.
Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving abilities.
Ability to anticipate operational challenges and develop recommendations or procedures to minimize or resolve issues.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate technical information to field personnel, customers, and management.
Ability to work effectively with Operations, Engineering, Sales, Repair and Maintenance, field personnel, and customers.
Proficiency with drilling analysis, data visualization, and Microsoft Office applications applicable to the position.
Ability to prioritize multiple projects and work independently with minimal supervision or as part of a team.
Willingness to travel as required.

Competencies

Strong analytical and technical problem-solving skills.
Strong understanding of drilling performance and optimization principles.
Ability to evaluate drilling parameters, BHA performance, and downhole behaviour to identify opportunities for improvement.
Ability to apply technical knowledge and field experience to improve drilling performance across individual wells and larger-scale projects.
Ability to communicate technical recommendations and lessons learned across Operations, Engineering, Sales, customers, and field teams.
Strong customer focus and the ability to develop effective professional relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Demonstrates initiative, sound judgment, accountability, and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced operational environment.

Why Join Us?
This is an opportunity to play a key technical role in drilling performance improvement, customer support, and applied drilling optimization. The Drilling Solutions Engineer will contribute directly to safe, efficient, and reliable well execution while working with experienced operations, technical, engineering, and field teams.

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
Description

We are hiring a data engineer to lead client delivery and build the next generation of engineers at Edge. This is a client‑facing leadership role. You will spend most of your time working directly with both public & private organisations working in the healthcare sector, leading project teams drawn from every grade, and coaching junior engineers face to face. If the phrase “forward‑deployed engineer” describes how you like to work, you will recognise this job.

Application Deadline: 18 October 2026

Department: Senior Data Engineers

Location: London

Compensation: £55,000 - £65,000 / year

Description

We are hiring a data engineer to lead client delivery and build the next generation of engineers at Edge. This is a client‑facing leadership role. You will spend most of your time working directly with both public & private organisations working in the healthcare sector, leading project teams drawn from every grade, and coaching junior engineers face to face. If the phrase “forward‑deployed engineer” describes how you like to work, you will recognise this job.

The engineering matters, and you will need to be a capable engineer. What makes someone excel here, though, is the ability to operate with clients and to develop people.

What it's like to work at Edge

The role is deliberately a mix of engineering and consulting. As a Senior Data Engineer you lead delivery with clients and develop the engineers around you, but you are still expected to be hands‑on: building pipelines, making architecture calls, and noticing when a build is drifting from good practice. You'll work closely with economists, data scientists and consultants, so the engineering always connects to the question the client is trying to answer.

The work is varied and often starts with a problem rather than a spec. We might be building data infrastructure for an NHS organisation, bringing together sensitive patient data safely so it can inform decisions, or creating a tool a client can run themselves. Because we work across the public and private health sector, no two projects look quite the same.

We are also small enough for people to shape what Edge does. Senior Data Engineers coach junior colleagues, contribute to bids and proposals, and help set how we engineer as a team. We set aside two training days each quarter, and gaps in the stack are something we train rather than screen out.

Edge is rated 4.9/5 on Glassdoor with 100% saying they would recommend the company. Recent reviews mention a supportive culture, interesting projects, personal development and lots of room to explore interests.

Key Responsibilities

  • Plan and manage small and medium-sized projects, or the technical workstream of larger ones, supported by more senior colleagues;
  • Produce client‑ready output: pipelines, models, reports and presentations that can go in front of a client as they stand;
  • Play an active part in client relationships: presenting, updating and handling harder conversations, with coaching from senior staff as you take on more;
  • Develop the junior engineers on your projects, coaching them through client interactions and managing their delivery as well as the technical work;
  • Handle sensitive data the way it should be handled, following our quality and information security practices, because being trusted with patient data is the foundation of everything we do;
  • Help the junior engineers around you get better, sharing what you know with the team and supporting new joiners as they find their feet;
  • Apply senior judgement to the technical work itself: noticing when a build is drifting away from good practice and doing something about it;
  • Look for the moments where good delivery opens the door to more work, and flag them to the senior colleague leading the account as well as contribute to bids and proposals.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

We greatly value diversity and would welcome applicants from a range of academic and professional backgrounds. While meeting all the stated job requirements can be beneficial, at Edge, we understand that diverse experiences and perspectives can bring great value to our work. So, if you're passionate about the work we do and share our values, we encourage you to apply, even if you don't meet every single criterion. The strongest applications will include examples of the following:

  • You have delivered data work in a client‑facing setting, such as consulting, an agency or an embedded role for 2-4 years, and are comfortable presenting your work and being challenged on it;
  • You have started developing others, whether through mentoring, onboarding or day‑to‑day coaching, and can give us an example of someone who is better at their job because of you;
  • You manage your own delivery well against deadlines and can plan and delegate work for a small team;
  • You have solid engineering foundations: strong SQL, plus experience with some of Azure or AWS, Databricks and Terraform. Gaps in the stack are fine, and we will train them;
  • You care about healthcare. Experience with the NHS or health data is a real advantage, and a passion for the sector is essential;
  • You take your own development seriously, come to your one‑to‑ones ready to work on something, and act on the feedback you get;
  • You are the kind of colleague people want on a project: straight with clients, considerate of the team, and someone who takes pride in working in the health & care sector;
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a technical discipline (computer Science, Engineering, mathematics or similar) expected.

Benefits

  • Discretionary annual bonus (typically averaging ~10% of base)
  • 25 days annual leave per year, including the option of buying up to 5 additional days.
  • Vitality Private health insurance and/or Bupa Cashplan
  • Two days training per quarter to support professional development
  • Cycle2Work scheme

We review applications on a rolling basis and invite candidates to interview as we go, so encourage you to apply early. If we receive a high number of strong applications, we may close the role before the advertised deadline.

title: Archaeological Technician
description:
The Archaeological Technician provides field and laboratory support for cultural resource management projects conducted throughout Florida and the southeastern United States. Responsibilities include archaeological survey, testing, excavation, monitoring, site documentation, data collection, and report preparation in support of compliance with federal, state, and local historic preservation regulations, including Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA) and Florida historic resource requirements.

The successful candidate will work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team under the supervision of senior archaeological staff while maintaining professional standards for archaeological investigations and documentation.

Work Environment

Archaeological Technicians routinely work outdoors in a variety of environments, including transportation corridors, undeveloped lands, wetlands, forests, coastal areas, agricultural properties, and active construction sites. Overnight travel and extended field assignments may be required depending on project needs.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Conduct archaeological field investigations including:

    • Phase I Cultural Resource Assessment Surveys (CRAS)

    • Phase II Archaeological Evaluations

    • Phase III Data Recovery excavations

    • Construction monitoring and archaeological inspections

  • Excavate shovel tests, test units, and block excavations in accordance with project specifications and regulatory requirements.

  • Identify, document, and record prehistoric and historic-period archaeological materials.

  • Complete field forms, notes, site records, maps, and photographic documentation.

  • Utilize GPS equipment, tablets, mobile GIS applications, and other field technologies to collect spatial data.

  • Assist with artifact processing, cleaning, cataloging, analysis, and curation activities.

  • Maintain accurate records and ensure quality control of field data.

  • Support preparation of technical reports and management summaries.

  • Adhere to company safety policies and project-specific health and safety requirements.

  • Travel extensively and work in remote locations throughout Florida.

  • Perform physical labor in various weather conditions and terrain, including wetlands, forests, agricultural lands, and urban environments.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Archaeology, Anthropology or related field.
  • Completion of an archaeological field school from an accredited institution or equivalent experience.
  • Basic knowledge of artifact identification, soils, and stratigraphy.
  • Familiar with Microsoft Office programs.
  • Able to use Global Positioning Systems
  • A valid driver’s license with acceptable violation history may be required.

  • Familiarity with cultural resource management practices and historic preservation regulations.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability to work effectively in a team environment.

  • Ability to pass background checks and gain access to secure project sites when required.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior archaeological field experience in Florida or the southeastern United States.

  • Familiarity with Florida prehistoric and historic archaeological resources.

  • Experience with Section 106 compliance projects.

  • Knowledge of Florida Master Site File documentation procedures.

  • Experience using GIS software, GPS equipment, ArcGIS Field Maps, Survey123, or similar platforms.

  • Experience conducting wetland, transportation, utility, or infrastructure-related surveys.

  • OSHA 10-Hour or OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER certification.

  • Boat operation experience or environmental field experience.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to walk 5 to 10 miles per day over uneven terrain.

  • Ability to dig shovel tests repeatedly throughout the workday.

  • Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds.

  • Ability to work outdoors in extreme heat, humidity, rain, insects, and other challenging environmental conditions typical of Florida.

  • Ability to stand, kneel, bend, stoop, and climb for extended periods.

Desired Knowledge and Skills

  • Understanding of Section 106 compliance and cultural resource investigations.

  • Knowledge of Florida archaeology, including prehistoric, contact-era, and historic resources.

  • Strong organizational and documentation skills.

  • Attention to detail and commitment to data quality.

  • Ability to adapt to changing field conditions and schedules.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and mobile data collection platforms.

title: Response Coordinator
description:
The George Washington University (GW) is committed to maintaining a positive climate for study and work, in which all individuals are judged solely on relevant factors, such as skill and performance, and can pursue their activities in an environment free from discrimination, harassment, and violence. The Office of Equal Opportunity supports this commitment by offering complaint resolution options, support to individuals involved in incidents, and education opportunities designed to prevent incidents and encourage prompt reporting.

Response Coordinator will play a critical role in a coordinated community response to discrimination and harassment based on protected characteristics, including sexual assault, dating and domestic violence, and stalking. The position’s primary role is to support GW faculty, staff, and students by initiating outreach to Complainants, Respondents, and third parties following a report of discrimination and harassment and to facilitate supportive measures for those impacted by these incidents. In addition, Response Coordinator will facilitate reasonable modifications for students experiencing pregnancy or related conditions. Response Coordinator directly reports to the Director of Response and Prevention.

JOB DUTIES

- Initiates outreach to community members who are impacted by discrimination and harassment including sexual assault, dating violence, domestic violence, and stalking.
- Meets with community members to gather preliminary facts underlying incidents, explain resolution processes offered through the Equal Opportunity Office, the availability of supportive measures, evidence preservation, and safety planning.
- Determines, in consultation with the Director of Response and Prevention and EO Coordinator, whether there is an immediate threat or safety concern for any individual and/or the campus community that should be escalated to the Behavioral Intervention Team (BIT), the Threat Assessment Team (TAT), and/or whether other immediate action should be taken.
- Describes complex resolution processes in detail and has the ability to answer questions pertaining to them.
- Provides free referrals to on-campus and community resources for healthcare, counseling, and other crisis management services.
- Files timely and anonymous reports with the Division of Safety & Operations pursuant to the Jeanne Clery Campus Safety Act.
- Collaborates with students, faculty, and staff to develop individualized safety plans to ensure the well-being of all parties involved in an incident.
- Provides trauma-informed support for Complainants, Respondents, and third parties while upholding core values related to compassion, impartiality, and fairness for all involved in the process.
- Ensures that all reports and supportive measures are thoroughly documented within the Office for Equal Opportunity’s case management system, Maxient.
- Leads training and orientation programming for GW staff, faculty, and students related to discrimination and harassment based on a protected characteristic, including sexual assault, dating and domestic violence, and stalking.

Performs other work duties as assigned. The omission of specific duties does not preclude the supervisor from assigning tasks logically related to the position.

title: Platform Reliability Engineer
description:
About the company

We are a young and fast-growing recruiting company with five years of experience working across Latin America and the United States. We partner closely with teams and founders to help them build strong, high-impact teams through recruitment, outsourcing, and team-building services.

Our culture is built on effective communication, trust, and transparency. We believe great work happens when people feel heard, supported, and empowered to grow. Today, our team is made up of more than 80 professionals working across different projects throughout the region, collaborating remotely and learning from each other every day.

About the role

We’re looking for a Platform Reliability Engineer to join a dedicated delivery pod building and running an internal agent platform on AWS Bedrock AgentCore for a global life sciences organization.

You’ll work as part of a team alongside the client’s engineers to build the reliability and observability foundations that other teams will use to develop and run their agents.

The role focuses on making the platform visible, measurable, and dependable. You’ll work across OpenTelemetry instrumentation, observability integrations, distributed tracing, SLOs, alerting, and cost monitoring for token and compute usage.

When an agent is slow, produces errors, or becomes unexpectedly expensive, your work will help the team understand what is happening, identify the source, and take action.

This is a named-team engagement, meaning the person proposed for the role will be the person who joins the project.

Responsibilities

  • Build OpenTelemetry instrumentation standards for agents, tools, and platform services, making them easy for engineering teams to adopt.
  • Integrate AgentCore Observability and Amazon CloudWatch with existing enterprise observability platforms such as Datadog, Splunk, Grafana, or similar tools.
  • Implement end-to-end distributed tracing across agent steps, model calls, tool calls, and multi-agent handoffs.
  • Define and implement SLOs, error budgets, and alerting strategies for latency, availability, and error rates.
  • Build reliable alerting that provides actionable signals without creating unnecessary noise.
  • Develop cost visibility and monitoring for token usage and compute spend across teams, agents, and environments.
  • Create dashboards, budgets, and alerts to identify unexpected increases in infrastructure or model usage costs.
  • Develop and maintain runbooks to support operational readiness and incident response.
  • Participate in incident response and troubleshooting, helping identify root causes and implement sustainable fixes.
  • Lead or contribute to post-incident reviews, turning findings into concrete improvements to the platform.
  • Work closely with client engineers and other technical stakeholders to turn observability and reliability data into actionable decisions.

Requirements

  • 6+ years of experience in SRE, Platform Reliability, Observability Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Strong hands-on experience with AWS in production environments.
  • Hands-on experience with OpenTelemetry, including SDKs, collectors, exporters, and distributed tracing.
  • Experience with Amazon CloudWatch and at least one enterprise observability platform such as Datadog, Splunk, Grafana, New Relic, or similar.
  • Experience defining and operating SLOs, error budgets, and alerting strategies.
  • Experience building AWS cost visibility and FinOps reporting, including Cost Explorer, Cost and Usage Reports (CUR), and tagging strategies.
  • Scripting or development experience with Python, Go, or TypeScript.
  • Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to turn system data into actionable decisions.
  • Clear communication skills and the ability to explain technical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Previous consulting experience.
  • Nice to have
  • Experience monitoring LLM or agent-based applications, including token usage, latency, errors, and quality signals.
  • Familiarity with LLM observability platforms such as Langfuse, Arize, or LangSmith.
  • Experience with AgentCore Observability.
  • Experience using Terraform or AWS CDK to provision and manage monitoring and observability infrastructure.
  • Experience working in pharma, life sciences, healthcare, or other regulated industries.
  • Previous experience or connections within the Life Sciences industry.

Benefits

  • People First culture
  • Referral Program
  • Free access to streaming platforms
  • Free access to Spotify Premium
  • GYM discount
  • Travel discount
  • E-Learning discount
  • Birthday-day gift
  • Points Program

title: Director - Manufacturing Engineering
description:
Specific Duties and Responsibilities:

Manufacturing Engineering

  • Manages the development, design, and manufacturing of assembly processes, tools and machines that will effectively and efficiently manufacture the company’s products.
  • Supervise purchasing new and used equipment, as well as design and construction methods for in-house equipment.
  • Act as product design consultant by working with Product Engineering to provide Manufacturing Engineering viewpoints.
  • Provide technical expertise and organization to defective paint/steel problems as well as R&D on new systems.
  • Responsible for floor plans, layouts and concepts of new buildings and upgrading of existing buildings and product manufacturing facilities.
  • Responsible for start-ups of new product manufacturing lines, debug and streamline productivity, ensure adequate raw materials and finished product quality.
  • Responsible for quality control decision making, including spot checks plant wide to determine improvement needs.

Controls Engineering

  • Responsible for the design, installation, optimization, and enhancement of electronic control systems and instruments to automate and monitor industrial processes.

Strategic and Tactical Planning

  • Responsible for providing strategic leadership regarding all issues relating to the manufacturing engineering function of the Company.
  • Assist the Vice President of Operations with developing long-term corporate strategies based on changing competitive, financial and market conditions.
  • Formalize and document a departmental plan that achieves strategic and tactical goals set for the Company, including managerial development and continuous improvement of staff.
  • Prepare capital and expense budgets, including expenditures guidance, and supervise the ongoing record of all expenditures.

Education/Experience:

Bachelor's degree (BS) in an engineering related field from four-year college or university plus 10 years minimum experience in a manufacturing engineering environment.

Certificates and Licenses:

PE preferred.

Metal Forming Experience:

10+ years experience in metal forming. Must have experience in the design of dies and tools for forming metal. Ability to troubleshoot manufacturing issues and concerns. Experience in developing training for engineers, maintenance, and production personnel. Experience in purchasing capital equipment and running capital projects.

Technical Skills

  • Metal Forming
  • Machine, Process, and Part Design
  • Plant Layouts and Material Flow Optimization
  • Automation and Manufacturing Technology Evaluation
  • Metrology
  • Continuous Improvement, Lean, and Structured Problem Solving
  • Data Collection, Analysis, and KPI Reporting
  • Creation of Work Instructions, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and Process Documentation
  • Safety Analysis, Ergonomics, and Risk Reduction
  • Project Plan Development, Management, and Execution
  • New Product Introduction and Engineering Change Implementation

Language Skills:

Ability to write reports, business correspondence, and procedure manuals. Ability to effectively present information and make presentations and respond to questions from groups of managers, clients, customers, and the public.

Mathematical Skills:

Ability to apply advanced mathematical concepts such as exponents, logarithms, quadratic equations, and permutations. Ability to apply mathematical operations to such tasks as frequency distribution, determination of test reliability and validity, analysis of variance, correlation techniques, sampling theory, and factor analysis.

Reasoning Skills:

Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions. Ability to interpret an extensive variety of technical instructions in mathematical or diagram form and deal with several abstract and concrete variables for problem solving.

Computer Skills:

To perform this job successfully, the qualified individual should be proficient in the use of Microsoft suite applications, CAD (SolidWorks preferred) and ERP Systems (JD Edwards preferred).

Supervisory Responsibilities:

Manages the manufacturing engineering and Controls function and carries out managerial responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include setting priorities, planning and assigning work, hiring, coaching, developing, and appraising performance, addressing complaints, resolving problems, and building a high-performing manufacturing engineering team aligned with business objectives. Ten years managerial experience required.

Core Values:

  • Deliver Service
  • Be Positive
  • Embrace Family
  • Be a Team Player
  • Show Integrity
  • Have Grit

    • Voluntary Life Insurance

title: Acquisition Program Security Analyst
description:
MANTECH seeks a motivated, career and customer-oriented Acquisition Program Security Analyst to support our USMC contract out of Quantico, VA.


MANTECH is responsible for assisting our Government customer and ensuring that material solutions developed or acquired by PAE-MC are system engineered, integrated, interoperable, and certified to provide the warfighter with equipment required to accomplish their mission.


Job Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Support the PAE-MC Acquisition Program Security Officer Lead (APSOL) to ensure that all technology protection document development, updating, and staffing are accomplished as depicted in the Program’s Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) and as described in the Department of Defense Technology and Program Protection Guidebook and the MCSC Acquisition Security Guidebook.
  • Participate in the various Security Working Groups to identify critical program information (CPI) and mission critical functions and components as required by DoD Directive 5200.39 and described in the DoD Instruction 5200.44.
  • Perform in-depth data analysis and configuration to identify, assess, and mitigate supply chain risks.
  • Act as a primary support analyst for the SCRM Lead, providing surge capacity during critical incidents, high-tempo operations, or urgent due diligence reviews. Assist in managing SCRM cases, tracking mitigation efforts, and preparing reports for program leadership.
  • Develop and update Program Protection Plans (PPP) as required by DoD Instruction 5000.83 and described in PDUSD Memorandum, “Document Streamlining – Program Protection Plan (PPP),” July 16, 2011 and the MCSC Acquisition Guidebook.

  • Bachelor’s Degree and at least 4 years of related experience (additional 2 years of experience may be substituted in lieu of degree.

  • Experience with planning, executing, and managing multiple projects
  • Ability to interpret policy and provide recommendations
  • Ability to work in a fast paced and stressful environment to meet critical timelines

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Basic understanding of Acquisitions
  • Critical Thinking
  • Problem Solving
  • Strong ability to coordinate with the APSL for all outside agency (e.g., Marine Corps Intelligence Activity (MCIA), Naval Criminal Investigate Service (NCIS), Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA), etc.) support to the programs.

Security Clearance Required:

  • Must have an active DoD TS/SCI

Physical Requirements:

  • Sedentary work

title: Regional Roots Program Specialist
description:
**The Regional Roots Program Specialist** will lead the continued development, implementation, delivery, assessment, and expansion of [_Regional Roots: Culinary Training to Enhance School Meals with Local Foods_](https://cals.cornell.edu/cornell-cooperative-extension/regional-roots), a flagship initiative of the Cornell Farm to School team within [Cornell Cooperative Extension’s Harvest NY program](https://cce.cornell.edu/harvest-new-york).

The Specialist will manage program planning, statewide implementation, partner engagement, training logistics, budgets, and continuous quality improvement. They will work closely with contracted culinary subject matter experts and other technical partners who develop and deliver hands-on instruction, ensuring trainings are well coordinated, responsive to participant needs, and aligned with program goals.

The Specialist will assess community and partner needs through surveys, focus groups, and other engagement strategies. They will use process and outcome evaluation to improve program quality, measure impact, and guide future development, and prepare reports that communicate accomplishments and meet sponsor and organizational requirements.

Working with the Farm to School Support Specialist, the Specialist will coordinate communications and outreach by developing and editing program materials, success stories, research summaries, website and social media content, and other outreach materials that increase the program’s visibility and share best practices. The Specialist will represent Regional Roots at meetings, conferences, and community events, building support for scratch cooking in school meals and increased procurement of New York-grown foods across the state.

**About the College, School, Unit or Department**

[The College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS)](https://cals.cornell.edu/) is a pioneer of purpose-driven science and Cornell University’s second largest college. We work across disciplines to tackle the challenges of our time through world-renowned research, education, and outreach. The questions we probe and the answers we seek focus on three overlapping concerns: We believe that achieving next-generation scientific breakthroughs requires an understanding of the world’s complex, interlocking systems. We believe that access to nutritious food and a healthy environment is a fundamental human right. We believe that ensuring a prosperous global future depends on the ability to support local people and communities everywhere. By working in and across multiple scientific areas, CALS can address challenges and opportunities of the greatest relevance, here in New York, across the nation, and around the world.

[Cornell Cooperative Extension (CCE)](https://cals.cornell.edu/cornell-cooperative-extension) provides the educational outreach functions for Cornell University’s role as New York State’s Land Grant University. Programmatically, Cornell Cooperative Extension connects the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS) and the [College of Human Ecology (CHE)](https://human.cornell.edu/) with 55 off-campus Associations, Integrated Pest Management, New York State Sea Grant, Area Specialists, and CCE New York City.

Harvest New York is an innovative Cornell Cooperative Extension team that focuses on workforce development and business expansion projects that increase profitability and investment in key sectors of New York’s agriculture industry throughout the State. Harvest New York Specialists respond to emerging issues and develop new opportunities using the research of Cornell University (both in Geneva at Cornell AgriTech and the Ithaca campus), the resources of Cornell Cooperative Extension and relationships with partnering organizations statewide. The four project areas covered by Harvest New York are: Food and Beverage Systems, Urban Agriculture, Climate Resiliency, and Emerging Crops.

**Hours, Location, and Travel**

This is a full-time, hybrid position based in New York State. The employee will typically work on-site two days per week at an agreed-upon location and may work remotely three days per week. The work location will be discussed with the selected candidate based on program needs and available space.

The usual schedule is Monday through Friday during business hours, with flexibility needed for school schedules, training events, and travel. Some early mornings, evenings, and occasional weekends may be required.

**Regular travel throughout New York State is an essential part of the role**. Travel will generally include day trips each week and overnight travel a couple of times per month, often for one night, with the frequency varying as the training schedule changes. The employee will help coordinate approximately 70 trainings annually but is not expected to attend every training. A fleet vehicle may be provided, or mileage will be reimbursed at the federal rate when a personal vehicle is used. Minimal out-of-state travel may also be required.

This is a full-time position. **This is a one-year term appointment that is contingent upon available work, funding, and performance.**

**Success Factors**

**You’ll thrive in this role if you:**

- **Build systems that support growth.** Use pilot findings to improve workflows, resources, and training coordination as Regional Roots expands.
- **Own the work and keep it moving.** Take initiative, manage competing deadlines and logistics, and keep your supervisor informed while working independently with a team spread across New York State.
- **Strengthen statewide partnerships.** Build productive relationships with school food authorities, culinary partners, Extension colleagues, and other stakeholders to support participation and program delivery.
- **Use evidence to improve and communicate results.** Apply evaluation data and participant feedback to refine the program, document outcomes, and communicate its impact clearly.

**What We Need**

- **A cover letter and resume outlining your interest and how your experience and goals align with the potential for mutual success in the role are required for consideration.**
- Bachelor’s Degree in Nutrition, Food Studies, Hospitality Management, Culinary Arts, or closely related field and 3 to 5 years relevant experience or equivalent combination.
- Ability to initiate, plan, organize, implement, teach, and evaluate informal educational programs.
- Effective written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong interpersonal skills with proven ability to work with diverse audiences in group and one-on-one settings.
- Ability to work effectively with advisory boards and committees, community-based organizations, and funding partners.
- Strong leadership and teamwork skills.
- Proven organizational and time-management skills.
- Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings and/or weekends, as appropriate.
- Proficiency with Windows-based software, including the internet and Microsoft Office Suite, including Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.
- **Must be able to meet the travel requirements of the position.**
- **Must have and maintain a valid and unrestricted NYS driver’s license and be cleared to drive for university business.**
- Ability to cultivate and develop inclusive working relationships with students, faculty, staff, and community members.

**If you have all those things, great! We have a few more things that we would prefer you to have, but it’s ok if you don’t.**

- Master’s Degree in Agriculture, Food Studies, Hospitality Management, Culinary Arts, or closely related field
- Knowledge of Farm to School programs.
- Experience leading program development, coordination, implementation, and continuous improvement for complex, multi-partner initiatives.
- Appreciation of agriculture as a business and as a lifestyle.
- Ability to learn the philosophy, objectives, and operation of an informal education system such as Cornell Cooperative Extension.

**Rewards and Benefits**

- This position is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement. Employees typically perform this role remotely 3 days per week and on-site 2 days per week. The university reserves the right to modify, suspend, revoke or terminate the hybrid work arrangement at any time.

- Our benefits programs include comprehensive health care options, generous retirement contributions, access to wellness programs, and employee discounts with local and national retail brands. We invite you to follow this link to get more information about our benefits: [Understand Your Benefits | Working at Cornell](https://hr.cornell.edu/understand-your-benefits).

- Our leave provisions include health and personal leave, three weeks of vacation and 13 holidays: Martin Luther King, Jr. Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and the day after, and an end of the year winter break from December 25-January 1. To offer greater flexibility for observing faiths and traditions we also offer two additional floating holidays. Learn more about our generous leave provisions: [Holiday and Accrued Time Off | Working at Cornell](https://hr.cornell.edu/about/employment-policy-practice/employment-policies/time-and-leaves/holiday-and-accrued-time)

- Cornell's impressive educational benefits include tuition-free Extramural Study and Employee Degree Program, tuition aid for external education, and Cornell Children's Tuition Assistance Program. Learn more about our extensive educational benefits: [Education Benefits | Working at Cornell](https://hr.cornell.edu/understand-your-benefits/education-benefits)

- Follow this link to learn more about the Total Rewards of Working at Cornell: [Total Rewards | Working at Cornell](https://jobs.hr.cornell.edu/us/en/total-rewards)

description:
Job Title: Sushi Clerk - Union
Department: Sushi
Job Region: Oregon / SW Washington
Reports to: Sushi Manager
Exemption Status: Non-Exempt
Union Represented: Yes, NSLU
Scheduling Requirements: This role supports a retail operation that is open seven days per week, including evenings, weekends, and holidays. Work schedules are based on business needs and may change seasonally or due to staffing demands. Reasonable accommodations related to scheduling will be considered in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.
Position Summary: Provides exceptional customer service and product guidance to customers while performing high-volume production of premium sushi products.
Position Responsibilities:

Performs production of sushi items, including prepping ingredients, rolling, and garnishing.
Prepares all sushi items strictly according to company recipes and artisanal standards to ensure consistency and quality.
Monitors product quality by handling ingredients according to company policy.
Executes department merchandising by stocking, rotating, and "facing" products with strict attention to quality and expiration dates.
Performs daily operational tasks, including department opening/closing, processing special orders, and maintaining accurate pricing and signage.
Performs logistical tasks such as receiving merchandise, verifying counts, and managing back-stock organization.
Maintains a sanitary environment by cleaning equipment and storage areas in accordance with food safety standards.
Monitors product integrity by identifying damaged or spoiled goods and reporting inventory discrepancies to management.
Communicates effectively with store leadership regarding safety, security, or customer service issues that may impact store operations.

General Responsibilities:

Prioritizes and completes assigned tasks based on department needs and changing business conditions.
Applies job-related judgment to address operational issues and routine decision-making in accordance with company policies and safety standards.
Works scheduled shifts based on business needs and maintains reliable attendance in accordance with company policy and applicable laws.
Uses company resources appropriately and complies with company policies, procedures, and standards of conduct.
Follows workplace safety practices and reports hazards, equipment issues, or compliance concerns promptly.
Provides responsive, courteous, and solutions-focused customer service by identifying customer needs, offering appropriate product guidance, and resolving concerns in accordance with company standards.
Communicates respectfully and collaborates with team members and leadership to support a productive work environment.
Contributes to an inclusive and respectful workplace by treating coworkers and customers fairly and using inclusive communication.
Performs basic arithmetic (addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division) for unit counts, weight tares, and handling transactions.
Reads and speaks English to ensure safety, follow recipes/schematics, and effectively communicate with customers.
Completes other duties as assigned.

Tools:

Industrial Kitchen: Rice cookers, sushi rolling and cutting equipment, fryer, and commercial refrigeration.
Cutting Tools: Knives, specialized vegetable slicers, and sharpeners.
Safety: Thermometers, industrial dishwashers, non-slip knives, cut-resistant gloves, standard PPE, and chemical sanitation kits.
Technology: Scales and standard office software.
Janitorial: Basic housekeeping and janitorial equipment.

Physical Requirements:

Stamina: Required to stand and walk for the duration of the shift (up to 8 hours).
Movement: Constantly required to stoop, bend, crouch, twist, pull, and reach. Frequent use of hands and wrists for grasping, squeezing, and fine motor tasks.
Dexterity: High level of manual dexterity and hand-eye coordination for intricate rolling, slicing, and garnishing.
Lifting: Must frequently lift and move up to 25 lbs. and occasionally up to 50 lbs.
Climbing: Occasionally required to climb stairs, step stools, or ladders.

Work Environment: This role is based in a dynamic grocery retail environment. Candidates should be prepared for the following conditions:

Physical Surroundings: Work involves navigating store floors, which may include wet or slippery surfaces. Depending on the specific location, navigating stairs or elevators may be required.
Climate & Temperature: Exposure to varying temperatures, including extreme cold while working in walk-in coolers and freezers, as well as outdoor conditions in all weather types.
Atmosphere: A moderate noise level is typical for this environment. There may also be exposure to dust, mold, gluten, fragrances, fumes, airborne particles, fresh fruits and vegetables, house plants, and flowers.

title: Certified Welding Inspector - CWI
description:
About Company:





Aegeus Inspection is a national leader in the Testing, Inspection, and Certification (TIC) sector, delivering non-destructive testing (NDT), inspection, and specialized workforce solutions across the aerospace, power, and oil & gas industries. We are a trusted partner dedicated to enhancing the quality, safety, and reliability of our clients’ assets and infrastructure while protecting the integrity of their operations.

Our success is driven by advanced technical expertise, an innovative mindset, and a team committed to operational excellence. With a strong and growing national footprint, Aegeus continues to expand in key markets, attracting top talent and creating opportunities for individuals who want to build meaningful, impactful careers.

Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veteran/Disability.


About the Role:

The Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) plays a critical role in ensuring the integrity and safety of welded structures within the professional, scientific, and technical services industry. This position is responsible for conducting thorough inspections and evaluations of welding processes, materials, and finished welds to verify compliance with industry codes and standards. The CWI collaborates closely with engineers, fabricators, and project managers to identify potential defects and recommend corrective actions, thereby preventing structural failures and ensuring quality assurance. This role demands a deep understanding of welding techniques, metallurgy, and inspection methods to maintain high standards of workmanship and safety. Ultimately, the CWI contributes to the successful completion of projects by guaranteeing that all welding activities meet regulatory and client specifications across diverse applications in the United States.

Company Perks

  • 100% Aegeus paid: Vision, Life, and Disability Insurance
  • Medical & Dental Insurance
  • 401K plan (with Company Matching)
  • Vacation Paid Time Off
  • Personal/Sick Pay
  • Per Diem for out of town expenses
  • Training & Development Programs

Pay range for this position is USD $45 to $60 per hour. Pay range for this job level is a general guideline only for States that enforces pay transparency and not a guarantee of compensation or salary. Additional factors considered in extending an offer include (but are not limited to) responsibilities of the job, education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, certifications, as well as internal equity, alignment with market data, applicable bargaining agreement (if any), or other law.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Certification as a Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) from the American Welding Society (AWS) or equivalent recognized body.
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in welding inspection or a related technical field within the professional, scientific, or technical services industry.
  • Strong knowledge of welding processes, metallurgy, and relevant codes such as AWS D1.1, ASME Section IX, and API standards.
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, welding procedure specifications (WPS), and inspection reports.
  • Excellent communication skills to effectively document findings and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Additional certifications such as Certified Radiographic Interpreter (CRI) or Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) certifications.
  • API 570 certification required.
  • Additional certifications such as API 510 and 653 preferred.
  • Experience with advanced inspection technologies including ultrasonic testing, magnetic particle testing, and radiographic testing.
  • Familiarity with quality management systems such as ISO 9001 and experience in auditing welding quality processes.
  • Prior experience working on large-scale infrastructure, oil and gas, or aerospace projects.
  • Proficiency with digital inspection tools and software for reporting and data management.

Responsibilities:

  • Perform detailed visual and non-destructive inspections of welds to assess quality and compliance with applicable codes and standards.
  • Review welding procedures, qualifications, and documentation to ensure adherence to project specifications and regulatory requirements.
  • Identify welding defects and discontinuities, document findings, and collaborate with fabrication teams to implement corrective measures.
  • Maintain accurate inspection records and prepare comprehensive reports for clients, regulatory bodies, and internal stakeholders.
  • Stay current with industry developments, standards, and best practices to continuously improve inspection techniques and processes.

Skills:

The CWI utilizes a comprehensive set of technical skills daily to evaluate weld quality and ensure compliance with stringent industry standards. Proficiency in interpreting complex engineering drawings and welding procedure specifications enables accurate assessment of welds against project requirements. Strong analytical skills are essential for identifying defects and determining their impact on structural integrity, while effective communication skills facilitate clear reporting and collaboration with project teams. Familiarity with non-destructive testing methods enhances the ability to detect hidden flaws without damaging components. Additionally, staying updated with evolving codes and inspection technologies ensures the CWI maintains a high level of expertise, contributing to continuous improvement in welding quality assurance.

title: Energy Efficiency Auditor
description:
Willdan Lighting & Electric, a division of Willdan Group Inc., is seeking an Energy Efficiency Auditor.

Willdan is a national leader in implementing energy efficiency programs. The exciting and growing energy efficiency sector provides Willdan employees with an opportunity to contribute to the clean energy economy. We are seeking motivated professionals to join our team on a new energy efficiency program across New York. For additional information, visit Willdan's website at . Willdan offers an excellent benefits package, a highly competitive total compensation plan (base salary + commission) and fosters a skilled, energized, and empowered workforce.

The Energy Efficiency Auditor is a key member of our outside sales team, working directly with commercial customers to identify energy-saving opportunities and help businesses take advantage of utility-sponsored incentive programs.This role focuses on business development, customer engagement, relationship building, and gathering site information needed to develop project proposals. The ideal candidate enjoys meeting new people, generating leads, conducting site visits, and helping customers navigate available energy efficiency programs. While a basic understanding of energy-saving technologies is helpful, this is primarily a sales-focused position rather than an engineering role.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Generate new business opportunities through door-to-door canvassing, networking, referrals, and follow-up on company-provided leads.
  • Meet with commercial customers to discuss energy efficiency programs, utility incentives, and available upgrade opportunities.
  • Build and maintain strong customer relationships through consistent communication and follow-up.
  • Conduct site visits to gather basic facility information, equipment details, and customer requirements needed for proposal development.
  • Collect and document project information, customer feedback, and site observations using company software platforms, including ViewPoint, ViewPoint DI, and Prospector.
  • Verify and update customer information to ensure accurate records.
  • Explain program eligibility requirements and assist customers with enrollment and participation in utility-sponsored programs.
  • Present proposals and help customers understand the potential benefits, incentives, and cost savings available through recommended improvements.
  • Maintain accurate records of customer interactions, site visits, sales activity, and follow-up schedules.
  • Participate in weekly and monthly sales meetings to review pipeline activity, prospecting efforts, and program goals.
  • Attend trade shows, community events, business networking events, and outreach activities as needed.
  • Consistently work toward achieving established sales goals and performance objectives.
  • Represent the company professionally while delivering excellent customer service.
  • Maintain and safeguard company-issued equipment.
  • Follow all company safety policies and procedures.

Job Requirements / Qualifications

    • High school diploma or equivalent.
    • Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
    • Self-motivated with a strong sales and customer-focused mindset.

    • Ability to organize and manage multiple customer opportunities simultaneously.
    • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and mobile technology, including tablets and laptops.
    • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.
  • Preferred
    • Associate degree or equivalent professional experience.
    • Experience in commercial sales, energy efficiency programs, construction services, facilities management, or related industries.
    • Familiarity with lighting, refrigeration, HVAC, insulation, or other energy-saving technologies.
    • Experience with CRM systems and sales tracking platforms.
    • Proven success generating leads and developing customer relationships.
  • Travel Requirements
    • Ability to travel locally throughout the assigned territory.
    • Travel may account for up to 70% of work time and may include driving, public transportation, rail, or occasional air travel as needed.
  • What We're Looking For
    • A motivated and outgoing sales professional who enjoys meeting new customers.
    • Strong relationship-building and communication skills.
    • Ability to gather information accurately and communicate customer needs effectively.
    • Goal-oriented individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment.
    • Team player with a positive attitude and strong work ethic.

### Description

**Preserve Nature. Enhance Neighborhoods. | Join Our Team as a Coordinator Public Works Projects**

**The Opportunity**

We are looking for a skilled, organized, and collaborative self-starter to step into the role of **Coordinator Public Works Projects** within the Open Space, Parks, and Golf division of the Community Services Department.

In this role, you will take the lead on a wide range of **capital improvement projects** that shape the outdoor spaces where our community gathers, plays, and connects with nature. From restoring scenic trails to renovating playgrounds and sports fields, you will help ensure Palo Alto’s open spaces, parks, and golf course remain safe, sustainable, and beautifully maintained.

If you have experience coordinating field-based construction and improvement projects and you are energized by work that makes a visible impact, this is your chance to bring ideas to life and contribute to the community in meaningful ways.

**About Us: Community Services Department**

The **Community Services Department (CSD)** enhances the quality of life in Palo Alto by providing safe, beautiful, and welcoming spaces, along with a wide range of recreational, cultural, and educational programs.

This position supports the Open Space, Parks, and Golf division:

- **Open Space** – Over 4,000 acres of protected natural lands, with trails, wildlife habitats, and native landscapes.
- **Park Services** – 162 acres of developed parkland, including playgrounds, athletic fields, landscaped areas, and gathering spaces.
- **Municipal Golf Course** –Baylands Golf Links 18-hole, links style course

Together, we care for the outdoor places that define Palo Alto’s character. They are spaces where the community celebrates milestones, find peace, stay active, and build connections.

**Why Work for the City of Palo Alto?**

Palo Alto, known as the birthplace of Silicon Valley is home to 69,700 residents and nearly 100,000 jobs. it’s a city that leads with purpose.

We are a full-service municipality with our own utilities, airport, and emergency services, backed by a AAA bond rating and a community that values innovation, sustainability, and public service. Here, you will join a high-trust, high-impact environment where your contributions matter and your ideas are welcomed.

**What You’ll Do**

As a project lead, you will coordinate and oversee a variety of capital improvement and maintenance projects, coordinate contractor activities, collaborate closely with the City’s purchasing team on procurement needs, and handle key administrative responsibilities. You will:

- Plan, schedule, and manage construction and infrastructure improvement projects from initiation through completion.
- Coordinate contractor activities across multiple maintenance and capital initiatives.
- Conduct site inspections to ensure safety, quality, and compliance with project plans and specifications.
- Lead or support project meetings with contractors, City staff, and stakeholders to track budgets, timelines, and deliverables.
- Identify and resolve project challenges to maintain progress and meet deadlines.
- Maintain, submit detailed records related to billing, scheduling, and project documentation.
- Assist with preparing budget requests and regular progress reports.
- Collaborate with community groups and volunteers to support improvement initiatives.

**Who We’re Looking For**

You are someone who enjoys seeing projects from planning to completion, thrives in a dynamic environment, and values collaboration as much as results.

You might be a great fit if:

- You enjoy working in indoors and outdoors settings making a tangible difference in your community.
- You are proactive and confident in leading complex projects with multiple stakeholders.
- You can read and interpret construction plans and bring a strong foundation in construction or project management.
- You are organized, detail orientated, adaptable, and capable of working independently and as part of a team.

You communicate clearly, listen well, and are comfortable working with a wide range of people, from internal teams to vendors, contractors, and community members.

**What You’ll Need**

**Education & Experience:**

- Education equivalent to two years of college coursework or related training.
- Three years of experience in public works operations, facility or landscape maintenance, or a related field, including at least two years in a lead role or overseeing contractor work.
- A Bachelor’s degree may substitute for up to two years of experience.

**License:**

- A valid California Driver’s License.

**Bonus Skills:**

- Familiarity with parks and trail maintenance, playground maintenance, resurfacing, site amenities, irrigation, turf care, or construction.
- Knowledge of safety regulations, public contracting, and field inspection practices.
- Familiar with the Palo Alto procurement process

**Work Environment**

This position primarily operates in an office setting, focusing on project management, procurement processing, scheduling, and coordinating with division managers to establish project priorities. The role also includes regular field visits, on-site project oversight, and negotiation with contractors, vendors, and stakeholders.

**Benefits Highlights**

- **CalPERS Pension** – Lifetime retirement income with up to 100% of your highest salary.
- **Fully Paid Medical, Dental & Vision** – Coverage for you and eligible dependents.
- **Six Weeks Paid Parental Leave.**
- **Up to $10,000/year in Childcare Assistance.**
- **Generous Time Off** – Up to 200 hours of vacation plus 13 paid holidays.
- **Commuter Perks**– Unlimited Bay Area transit with Clipper BayPass, including Caltrain, BART, VTA, MUNI, and more

Visit our [Careers Page](https://www.governmentjobs.com/careers/paloaltoca) to learn more and view [MOAs](https://www.paloalto.gov/Departments/Human-Resources/Labor-Agreements-and-Salary-Schedules) between the City and its employee groups.

- **Final Interviews:** Week of November 9, 2026 _(subject to change)_

Candidates selected to move forward will be notified directly of any changes to the interview schedule.

**Ready to Make an Impact?**

Apply today and help shape the open space, parks, and golf course that make Palo Alto an extraordinary place to live and visit.

Essential and other important responsibilities and duties may include, but are not limited to, the following:
